translations.text: The vision that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, who ruled Judah.
Listen, heaven, and pay attention, earth, for the Lord has spoken and said: “I bore children and raised them, but they rebelled against me.”
“An ox knows its owner, and a donkey knows its feeding trough and its master’s house. But Israel does not know me, and my people have not sought me.”
Woe to the sinful nation, a people full of wrongdoing, offspring of evildoers, corrupt children! You have abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
Why, then, are you struck while you keep adding sin to sin? Every head is sick, and every heart is sorrowful.
From foot to head there is nothing but wounds, bruises, and festering sores. There is no medicine to heal them; they are neither bandaged nor anointed.
Your land is desolate, and your cities are burned with fire. An enemy consumes your fields before your eyes; a foreign enemy ruins and plunders them.
Daughter Zion will be left like a grain watchman’s hut, like a vineyard watchman’s shelter, like a besieged city.
If the Lord of hosts had not left us offspring, we would have become like Sodom and resembled Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom! Pay attention to the law of God, people of Gomorrah!
“What use to me are your many sacrifices?” says the Lord. “I have had enough sacrifices of rams and the fat of sheep. I do not desire the blood of cattle and goats.”
“Even if you bring them, do not appear before me. Who required this from your hands? Do not walk through my courtyard again.”
“Even if you bring fine flour, it is worthless, and your incense is unclean.”
“My soul hates your new moons and your festivals.”
“When you raise your hands toward me, I turn my eyes away from you. Even if you multiply your prayers, I will not listen to you, because your hands are full of blood.”
Wash yourselves and be clean. Remove the evil of your souls from before my eyes; abandon your wickedness.
Learn to do good. Seek righteousness and rescue the oppressed. Give justice to the orphan and vindicate the widow.
“Come, let us argue our case,” says the Lord. “Even if your sins are like scarlet, I will make them white as snow. Even if they are like crimson, I will make them clean as wool.”
“If you are willing and listen to me, you will eat the blessings of the land.”
“But if you refuse to listen to me, the sword will devour you.” For the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
How the faithful city of Zion has become a prostitute! She was full of justice, and righteousness lived within her, but now there are thieves and murderers.
Your gold is debased, and your wine sellers add water to the wine.
Your rulers are faithless, partners of thieves. They accept and love bribes and want to pervert justice. They do not listen to the widow or give justice to the orphan.
Therefore the Lord of hosts says this: Woe to the mighty men of Israel! My wrath against my adversaries will not cool, and I will take vengeance on my enemies.
“I will bring my hand against you and refine you with heat. I will burn up the faithless and remove all wrongdoers from you.”
“I will appoint your rulers for you as in former times, and your counselors as at the beginning.”
For your captives will be saved through righteousness and acts of mercy.
Sinners and lawless people will be crushed together, and all who have abandoned the Lord will perish.
They will be ashamed of the gods they devised for themselves, and they will be ashamed of the sanctuaries they loved.
They will be like a terebinth tree that has shed its leaves, and like a garden that has no water.
Their strength will be like a stalk of [?], and their deeds like burning coals. Sinners and lawless people will burn together, and they will have no one to put out their fire.
The word that came to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
In the last days, the mountain of the Lord and the house of the Lord will appear on the mountaintops and will be raised above the hills, and all nations will go to it.
Many nations will come and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob. They will tell us his way, and we will walk [?] in the Lord’s footsteps.”
He will judge between the nations and rebuke many nations.
And now, house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord.
For he has rejected his people Israel, because they are full of their old practices, practicing divination like the Philistines, and many children of foreign nations have been born to them.
Their country is full of gold and silver, and their treasures cannot be counted. Their land is full of horses, and their armies cannot be counted.
Their land is full of the idols they made with their own hands, and they have bowed down to what they made with their own fingers.
People have been brought low, and humanity has been humbled, and he will not forgive them.
And now, enter the rocks and hide in the hollows of the earth, from the terror of the Lord’s presence, from his majesty and the glory of his power, when he rises to crush the earth.
For the eyes of the Lord are exalted, but humanity is lowly.
For the day of the Lord of hosts is against everyone who is proud, arrogant, and haughty, and against everyone who is lofty and exalted, and he will bring them low.
It is against all the tall, lofty trees of Lebanon and against all the oaks of Bashan.
It is against all the tall mountains and all the lofty hills.
It is against every tall tower and every fortified wall.
It is against all the ships on the sea and against all the idols of the gods.
All people will be brought low, and human pride will fall. The Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
They will hide all the idols they made with their own hands.
They will take them into caves, into cracks in the rocks, and into the hollows of the earth, away from the majestic presence of the Lord and the glory of his power, when he rises to crush the earth.
At that time people will cast out the unclean idols of gold and silver that they made to worship what is worthless.
So that they may enter the hollows of the earth and the cracks in the rocks, away from the majestic presence of the Lord and the glory of his power, when he rises to crush the earth.
Look, the Lord of hosts will remove from Jerusalem and Judah the strong and their strength, the sustaining power of grain and the sustaining power of water.
And the strength of a mighty warrior, the strength of a fighting man, the ruler, the prophet, the wise man, and the elder.
And the ruler, the counselor, the skilled master carpenter, the discerning person, and the attentive listener.
I will appoint young men as their rulers, and mockers will govern them.
People will fall upon people, man upon man, and each upon his neighbor. The young will clash with the old, and the lowly with the honored.
A man will seize his neighbor, a member of his father's household, and say to him, “If you have clothing, become my ruler and provide me with food.”
At that time he will answer him and say: I will not be your ruler, for I have neither food nor clothing in my house. I will not be a ruler of this people.
For Jerusalem has passed away, and Judah has fallen. Their speech is rebellious, for they deny the Lord.
For now their glory has been disgraced, and their faces have been put to shame. Their sin has stood against them; like the sin of Sodom, it has appeared and become known against them.
And they said: Let us bind the righteous man, for he is troublesome and burdensome to us.
Woe to the sinner because of his evil! They will receive according to the evil deeds of their hands.
My people, your rulers wear you out, and women rule over you. My people, those who call you blessed lead you astray and erase the tracks of your feet.
But now the Lord will rise to judge, and he will make his people stand before him so that he may bring his case against them.
The Lord himself will come with the elders of his people and with their rulers, and he will say, “You have burned my vineyard, and the plunder taken from the poor is in your houses.”
Why do you oppress my people and shame the face of the poor?

Thus says the Lord: “Because the daughters of Zion have become proud and walk with their necks stretched out, flirting with their eyes, scuffing their feet, dragging the hems of their clothes, and dancing as they go,”
the Lord will disgrace the prominent daughters of Zion, and the Lord will strip off their clothing.
On that day the Lord will take away their splendid clothes, their ornaments, their chains, and their bracelets;
their diadems, their pearls, and their neck ornaments;
their necklaces, their rings, their headdresses, and their purple clothes;
their silk clothes and their brocade clothes;
their gold garments and their garments of [?];
all their attire and their veils of [?].

Instead of the fragrance of your perfume, you will have dust; instead of your golden belt, a rope girdle. Instead of the golden diadem on your head, baldness will come upon you because of your evil deeds. Instead of your purple clothing, put on sackcloth.
Your eldest son, whom you love, will fall by the spear, and your warriors in battle.
The chests holding your ornaments will be put to shame and mourn. You will be left alone, and they will strip you bare on the ground.
Seven women will seize one man and say to him, “We will eat our own food and wear our own clothes. Only let us be called by your name, and take away our disgrace.”
On that day the Lord will shine upon the earth according to his glorious purpose, so that those who remain of Israel may be protected and honored.
Those who remain in Zion and those left in Jerusalem will be called holy—all who are recorded to live in Jerusalem.
For the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons of Zion and her daughters, and he will cleanse the blood from among them by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of purification.

He will come, and all will be on the roads to Mount Zion. A cloud will overshadow everything around it by day, and by night there will be something like smoke and the light of a burning fire, and it will be covered with glory.
It will be a shade from the heat and a covering under which to shelter from dew and rain.
I will sing to you a song for my beloved, whom I love. My beloved had a vineyard in a well-watered land, in its corner.

I put a fence around it, cleared it, and planted choice Sorek vines in it. I built a watchtower in its midst and dug a winepress for it. Then I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
And now, people of Judah and you who live in Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard.
What more, then, shall I do for my vineyard that I have not done for it? Look, I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
And now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will tear down its fence, and they will plunder it. I will remove its wall, and it will become a place to be trampled.
I will abandon it; it will not be pruned or dug. Grass and thorns will grow in it, and it will become waste. I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.

For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel—hosts, the house of Israel [?]. And the people of Judah are the new planting he loved. I waited for them to practice righteousness, but they practiced injustice; instead of justice there was an outcry.
Woe to those who join house to house and bring field next to field, so that they may seize their neighbors’ fields! They want to take the whole land for themselves alone.
For this has been heard in the ears of the Lord of hosts: Even if you multiply houses, they will be plundered. Though they are large and beautiful, no one will live in them.
For ten yoke of oxen will accomplish nothing and will not produce a single jar; and whoever sows six will bring in a third.
Woe to those who go early in the morning to the drinking house, spend the day drinking, and are inflamed by wine!
They drink wine while singing to the lyre, drum, and flute. They drink wine but do not consider the work of the Lord or look at the deeds of his hands.
And now my people have been taken captive because they did not know the Lord, and their folly has increased through hunger and thirst for water.
Death has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth wide, leaving nothing behind. The honored, the great, the rich, and sinners will descend into it.
People will be brought low, humanity will be humbled, and the eyes of the proud will be lowered.
The Lord of hosts will be exalted in righteousness, and the holy God will be glorified in justice.
They will graze like oxen that have been taken captive. They will graze like sheep in a field, seeking food in their pasture.
Woe to those who drag their sin like a long rope and bind their wrongdoing like an ox’s yoke!
They say, “Let him act quickly so that we may see! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come, so that we may know it!”
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who call light darkness and darkness light, who call sweet bitter and bitter sweet!
Woe to those who are clever at evil and say, “We are like the wise!”
Woe to the mighty who drink wine, and to the strong who make their strong drink stronger!
They acquit the sinner and accept bribes; they wrong the righteous and conceal his righteousness.

Because of this, just as straw burns in the coals of a fire and is consumed by the flame, so their root will rot, and their blossom will rise like dust. For they rejected the law of the Lord of hosts and provoked the word of the Holy One of Israel.
The Lord of hosts became greatly angry with his people. He raised his hand against them and struck them.
Now he will raise a signal over distant nations and draw them from the ends of the earth. Look, they are coming quickly, rushing forward!
They will neither hunger nor thirst; they will neither grow weary nor sleep. They will not loosen their belts from their waists, and the straps of their sandals will not break.
Their arrows are sharp, and their bows are strung. Their horses’ hooves are like hard stone, and their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.
They roar like lions and rise like young lions. They seize and roar like a wild beast coming out, and there is no one to rescue them.
On that day they will wail over them like the sound of a turbulent sea. They will look upon the land and see thick darkness, and they will be distressed.
Then, in the year when King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, high and lofty, and the house was full of his glory.
And seraphim stood around him. Each had six wings: with two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
They called to one another and said, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts! The whole earth is full of your glory.”
Then the door lintel was lifted up by the sound of those calling, and the house filled with smoke.

And I said, “Oh, wretched me! For I am a human being, and I am terrified, because my lips are unclean, and I live among a people whose lips are unclean. And now I have seen the King, the Lord of hosts, with my own eyes.”
Then one of the seraphim was sent to me, holding in his hand a coal that he had taken from the altar with tongs.
He touched my lips and said to me, “Look, I have touched your lips with this and taken away your sins, and he will cleanse you of your guilt.”
Then I heard the voice of the Lord of hosts saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people?” And I said, “Here I am, my Lord. Send me.”
And he said to me, “Go to this people and tell them: ‘You will indeed hear, but you will not understand; you will indeed see, but you will not know.’

For this people have made their hearts dull and their ears deaf so that they do not hear. They have covered their eyes so that they do not see with their eyes or hear with their ears or understand with their hearts or turn back and receive mercy.”
And I said, “Until when, Lord?” He said to me, “Until the cities are devastated and there is no one left living in the houses, and the land is left alone like a wilderness.
Then the Lord will send the people far away, and those who remain on the land will be many.
They will be a tenth, and again they will plunder it. It will be like a terebinth tree and like the trees of Lebanon when their leaves fall.”

In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to wage war against Jerusalem, but they were unable to conquer it.
The house of David was informed, “Aram has joined forces with Ephraim.”
And the Lord said to Isaiah, “Go out and meet Ahaz, you and your son Jashub, at the upper pool, on the road to the fuller’s field.
Tell him, ‘Be careful and remain quiet. Do not be afraid, and do not let yourself be terrified by these two smoking pieces of wood, for I will show mercy after I have punished in my anger.
The son of Aram and the son of Remaliah have plotted an evil plan against you.
They said, “Let us go up against Judah and confront them and turn them to our side.” And they said, “Let us make the son of Tabeel king over them.”
This is what the Lord of hosts says: “Their plan will not stand, and it will not happen for them.
But the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin.
And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah.”’”
And the Lord spoke again to Ahaz and said to him:
“Ask for a sign for yourself from the Lord your God, either in the depths or in the heights.”
And Ahaz said, “I will not ask, and I will not put the Lord my God to the test.”
And he said, “Listen, house of David! Is it a small thing in your eyes to provoke people, that you also provoke God?
Look, then: because of this, the Lord will give you a sign.
Honey and butter will be his food before the child knows good and evil.
For before the child knows good and evil, he will reject evil and choose what is good.
The Lord will bring upon you, your people, and your father's house days that have not come since Ephraim brought the king of Persia in from Judah.
At that time the Lord will summon the flies that rule over half the river of Egypt, and the bee that is on the border of the land of Persia.
They will come and settle in the lowlands, in all the ravines, in the hollows of the earth, in all the cracks in the rocks, and in all the trees.
At that time the Lord will shave the king of Persia's head and hair with a hired razor from beyond the river, and will cut off his beard.
At that time a person will keep a heifer from among his cattle and two sheep.
Then milk will be plentiful, and those who remain in the land will feed on honey and butter.

At that time vines will flourish in all the ravines, and there will be a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels. But afterward the whole land will again become desolate and be filled with thorns and briers.
People will enter it with arrows and bows, because the whole land will become desolate and be filled with thorns and briers.
They will plow every hill for cultivation.
And the Lord said to me: Take a large, new sheet of papyrus and write on it with a human pen these words: Quickly summon and plunder.
I called faithful men to witness for me: Uriah and Zechariah son of Berechiah.
I went to the woman, the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son.
For before the child knows how to name his father and mother, the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried away before the king of Persia.
The Lord spoke to me again, once more.
Because this people rejected the water of Siloam, which flows quietly, and want to find Rezin son of Remaliah to make him king over you,
therefore, look: the Lord will bring upon you the abundant and mighty waters of the river—the king of Persia in all his glory.
He will destroy the brave man from Judah and bring the mighty to an end.
Know this, nations, and be defeated! Listen, as far as the ends of the earth, and be defeated, you mighty ones! Even if you grow strong again, you will again be defeated.
Even if you devise a plan, the Lord will overturn your plan. Whatever you say will not come about for you, because God is with us.
This is what the Lord of hosts said as he disciplined me with his strong hand and admonished me with the words of his mouth: “Do not walk in the way of this people.”
Do not say, “It is terrible.”
Honor the Lord as holy, and he will be the one you fear.
And if you trust in him, he will sanctify you and will not make you stumble like a stumbling stone or like a rock that makes you slip.
Because of this, many among them will stumble and fall and be crushed; they will approach and ensnare people.
At that time those who seal up the law so that it cannot be learned will grow strong.
He will say, “I will wait for the Lord, who has turned his face away from the house of Jacob, and I will put my trust in him.”
Here I am, with the children whom the Lord has given me.

If there are people who tell you, “Consult those who speak to you from beneath the earth and those who speak vainly through divination and utter lies from their hearts,” do not the nations consult their idols, seeking answers about the living from the dead?
For he gave a law to help them, so that they might say, “The matter is not like this,” and give no gift on its account.
Because of this, famine will come upon you. When you are hungry, you will grieve and speak evil against angels and rulers, and you will look upward into heaven

and downward to the earth. You will see thick darkness and suffer great distress. You will suffer pain and conceive. It will grow dark before you, and you will not see. The distressed person will not escape until his time arrives.
Do this quickly, and drink quickly, land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the rest of the coastal region, the region beyond the Jordan, and Galilee of the nations.
The people who live in darkness have seen a great light. Light has shone upon those who live in a land of darkness and the shadow of death.
You have brought down with joy the one who increases the people. They rejoice before you like those who rejoice at harvest and like those who divide plunder.
For the yoke laid upon them has been broken, and also the rod upon their necks. For he turned back the rod of those who exact payment and removed those who oppress them, as in the days of Midian.
Gather all the garments collected by theft, and exact clothing in exchange. They will want to burn it with fire.

For a child has been born to us; a son has been given to us. Authority rests upon his shoulder, and his name will be called Messenger of Great Counsel. For I will bring peace to the angels, and his life.
Greatness is before him, and there is no end to his peace. His kingdom will be established upon David’s throne, and he will uphold it with righteousness and justice, from now and forever.
The Lord sent death upon Jacob, and it came upon Israel.
All the people of Ephraim and those who live in Samaria will know, in their disgrace—those who speak with arrogance in their hearts.
The bricks have fallen. Come, let us quarry stone; let us cut down sycamores and cedar as a foundation for ourselves.
The Lord will crush those who stand on Mount Zion and scatter the enemy:
the Syrians from the east and the foreigners from the west, who devour Israel, opening their mouths wide against them.
The people did not turn back until they were struck, and they did not seek the mighty Lord.
The Lord cut off from Israel head and tail, great and small, in a single day.
The elder and those who show favoritism are the head, and the prophet who teaches wrongdoing is the tail.
Those who call this people blessed go astray, and they lead them astray so that they make them sin.
Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, nor will he have mercy on their orphans and widows, for they are all wicked and hostile, and every mouth speaks injustice.
Sin burns like fire, like dry straw consumed by fire. It blazes like grass in the wilderness and consumes everything around the hills.
The scourge of the Lord’s wrath burns the whole earth. The people will be like fuel for the fire, and no one will have mercy on his brother.
He turns to the right because he is hungry; he eats on the left, but no one is satisfied, even as he eats the flesh of his own arm.
Even with this, his wrath has not turned away; his hand is still raised.
Woe to those who write an evil decree!
They deny justice to the poor and deny justice to the needy among my people. They rob widows and plunder orphans.
What will they do on the day of their punishment, when their distress comes upon them from far away? To whom will you flee for refuge, and who will help you? Where will you leave your wealth?
So that you do not fall into disgrace. Yet despite all this, his anger has not turned away; his hand is still raised.
Woe to the Persians, the rod of my anger, with a scourge in their hands!
I will send my scourge against my sinful people. I will command my people to plunder them and take their possessions, to trample their cities and make them like dust.
He, however, is not as they reckoned in their hearts, nor is he in his soul as they imagined. Rather, he will destroy many nations by his plan.
And even if they say to him: Are you alone a ruler?
He says, “Have I not taken the land above Babylon, and Calneh, where the fortress was built? I have also taken Arabia, Damascus, and Samaria.
Just as I took these, so I will take everything on my campaign.
As I dealt with Samaria and the work of her hands, so I will also deal with Jerusalem and her idols.”
Then, when the Lord has finished doing all this on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, the Lord will come against the arrogant heart of the ruler of Persia, against his eyes and his wealth.
For he said, “By my strength I will act, and by my wise counsel I will conquer nations on my campaign and plunder their forces.
I will shake the cities that lie within it, gather the whole world, and turn it over in my hand like a child and like an egg. No one will escape me, and no one will oppose me.”
Do they praise an axe when no one chops with it? Does a saw exalt itself when no one saws with it, like someone who takes up a rod and a piece of wood?
Because of this, the Lord will send disgrace upon your glory and a fire upon your wealth that will burn and blaze.
The light of Israel will become a fire, and they will be made holy by a fire that burns and blazes and devours trees like grass.
On that day, mountains, hills, and trees will perish, and it will consume soul and body. Whoever flees will be like someone fleeing from a blazing flame of fire.
Those that remain among them will be so few that a child can write them down.
On that day, those who remain of Israel and those who have escaped from Jacob will no longer trust those who led them astray. Instead, they will truly rely on the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
Those who remain of Jacob will find strength in the Lord.
Even if the number of the children of Israel is like the sand of the sea, those who remain will be saved.
For the word is completed and cut short in righteousness.
Therefore the Lord of hosts says this: My people who live in Zion, do not fear Persia, for he will strike you with a rod. For I will bring my scourge upon you, so that you may see the road to Egypt.
For in a little while, my anger and my scourge against their plans will subside.
And the Lord will bring a scourge upon them like the scourge of Midian in the land of affliction; and his spear will be directed toward the sea route and along the road toward Egypt.
On that day, the yoke will be removed from your neck and fear will be removed from you. The yoke will be shattered from your shoulders.
For he will enter the city of Ai, pass through Megiddo, and leave his equipment in Michmash.
He will cross the lowland, and when he reaches Ai, Ramah, the city of Saul, will be afraid.
The daughter of Gallim will flee, and it will be heard in Enson and in Anathoth.
Madmenah and those who live in Gebim will be alarmed.
He will entreat them concerning his path, so that they may be with his hand; and they will entreat him for the mountain of the daughter of Zion and for the hills of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord of hosts will throw the nobles into confusion by his power. He will crush the great with humiliation, and the great will be brought low.
The tall ones will fall by the axe, and Lebanon will fall with its tall cedars.
A shoot will come out from the root of Jesse, and a flower will rise from his stump.
The Spirit of the Lord will rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and knowledge, the spirit of strength and counsel, the spirit of understanding and righteousness.
And the spirit of the fear of the Lord will fill him.
But he will judge with gentle judgment and rebuke the nobles of the earth. He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and the sinner with the breath of his lips.
He will gird his waist with righteousness and wrap his sides with uprightness.
Wolves will graze with sheep, and a leopard will rest with a young goat. Cattle will graze with lions, and a little child will lead them.
Cattle and bears will graze together, and their young will nestle together. A lion will eat straw like an ox.
A little child will put his hand into the hole of an earth snake and into the den of vipers.
There will be no one to hurt him, and no one will be able to harm him or anyone else on my holy mountain, for the knowledge of the Lord has filled everything, like abundant water covering the sea.
On that day the root of Jesse will stand, and the one appointed will be a messenger to the nations. The nations will trust in him, and his resting place will be glorious.

On that day the Lord will again reveal his hand, to recover the remnant of those who remain from the nations, whom Persia, Egypt, Babylon, Ethiopia, and Elam have left, and those from the east and the west.
He will show a sign to the nations and gather those who remain of Israel. He will gather the scattered people of Judah from the four ends of the earth.
He will remove Ephraim's jealousy, and Judah's enemies will perish.
They will fly in the Philistines' ships on the sea. Together they will plunder those from the east and Edom. They will first lay their hands on Moab, and they will first subdue the Ammonites.
And the Lord will dry up the sea of Egypt and stretch out his hand over the river with a powerful wind. He will strike seven ravines so that people may cross them wearing sandals.
There will be a passage for my people who remain in Egypt, and it will be for Israel as it was when they came out of Egypt.
And on that day you will say, “I praise you, Lord, because you were angry with me, but you turned away your punishment and again had mercy on me.”
Look, my God and my Savior! I will trust in him. I will live and [?] will not fear, for the Lord is my glory and my protection, and he has become my Savior.
You will draw water joyfully from the well of life.
On that day you will say, “Praise the Lord and call upon his name. Tell the nations of his glory, and remember that his name is exalted.”
Praise the name of the Lord, for he has done great things. Proclaim this throughout the earth.
Let those who live in Zion rejoice and be glad, for the Holy One of Israel is exalted in your midst.
The vision that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Babylon.
Raise a banner on the mountains of the wilderness. Raise your voices and strengthen your hands. Let the rulers open the gates.
I will command them, and I will bring my holy ones. I will bring those who prosper. Rejoicing, they will come together and carry out my wrath and humiliate them.
The clamor of many nations on the mountains, like that of many nations, armies, and kings gathered together! The Lord of hosts has commanded the nations of warriors to come.
From a distant country, from the ends of the earth, the foundation of heaven: the Lord and his warriors will destroy the world.
Wail, for the day of the Lord is near, and destruction will come from the Lord.
And because of this, every hand will grow weak and every soul will be terrified.
And the leaders will be thrown into confusion, and pain will seize them like a woman giving birth. They will fight among themselves; they will be tormented, and their faces will blaze like fire.
For look, the day of the Lord is coming, full of wrath and punishment, to destroy the world and wipe out its many sinners.
Then the stars of heaven, those of Orion, and the whole heavenly realm will not shine. The sun will grow dark at its rising, and the moon will not shine.
Then I will command disaster against the whole world and against sinners. I will bring down the pride of sinners and humiliate the arrogant in their boastfulness.
And those who remain will be more precious than gold and silver, and a person will be more precious than a sapphire gem.
For heaven will be shaken, and he will shake the earth from its foundation because of the wrath and punishment of the Lord of hosts, when his wrath comes.
Those who survive will be like a fleeing gazelle and like a lost sheep, with no one to gather it or turn it back. Each person will return to his own country.
Those who are scattered will die, and those who are gathered together will fall by the spear.
Their children will be dashed to pieces, their houses will be plundered before their eyes, and their wives will be dragged away.
Look, I will stir up the Persians against you. They do not desire gold or care about silver.
They will crush and destroy the lives of young men. They will have no mercy on your little ones, and their eyes will not spare your children.
Babylon, which the kings of Persia call glorious, will become like Sodom and Gomorrah, which God overthrew.
She will never exist again or be inhabited from generation to generation. No one will enter her for many generations. Arabs will not pass through her, and shepherds will not rest within her.
Wild animals will live there, and her houses will be filled with [?]. Sirens will rest within her, and demons will dance there.
Those whose feet have hooves like cattle will live there, and [?] will breed there in their houses.

And all this will happen quickly and will not be delayed. The Lord will have mercy on Jacob and will choose Israel again. They will rest in their own land, and foreigners will join them and be added to the house of Jacob.

The nations will take them and bring them into their land. They will divide them among themselves, and they will become numerous in that land. They will be male and female slaves there. Those who took them captive will become captives, and those who enslaved them will become slaves.
On that day the Lord will give you rest from your suffering, your distress, and the bitter slavery in which you served them.
On that day you will take up this saying against the kingdom of Babylon: “How the oppressor has been brought down! How the tormentor has been brought down!”
For the Lord has shattered the yoke of sinners and the yoke of rulers.
The Lord struck the nations with the scourge of his wrath. He did not spare the nations from the scourge of his wrath.
Then the whole earth rested in safety and cried out with joy.
And the trees of Lebanon and the cedars of Lebanon will rejoice over you: “Since you were laid down, no one has come up to cut us down.”
Sheol below grew bitter, and they welcomed you. All the mighty ones who ruled the earth rose with you, those who raised all the kings of the earth from their thrones.
They will all answer you and say, “You too have been taken captive like us! Your counsel too has been defeated!”
Your great rejoicing has fallen from your glory into Sheol. Decay is spread beneath you, and worms are your covering.
How the morning star, which rises at dawn, has fallen from heaven! He who sends to all the nations has been crushed to the earth.
But you said in your heart, “I will ascend into heaven and set my throne above the stars of heaven. I will sit above a high mountain, among the high mountains toward the south.
I will ascend above the clouds and become like the Most High.”
But now you will be hurled into Sheol and descend to the foundations of the earth.
Those who see you will be astonished and say, “Is this the man who devastated the land of Zion and its kings?
He made the whole world a wilderness, destroyed its cities, and did not release its prisoners.”
All the kings of the nations were laid to rest, each in honor in his own house.
And you too will be cast into the mountains like an unclean corpse, with the many corpses of those pierced by the spear, who go down into Sheol.
Like a garment covered with blood that is not clean, so you too are not clean.
Prepare your children for slaughter because of their fathers’ sins, so that they will not rise up and inherit the earth, and so that they will not multiply slaughter on the earth.
“I will rise up against them,” says the Lord of hosts, “and destroy their descendants, their name, and those who remain of them.
I will make Babylon a place where birds live, and she will become nothing. I will make her a [?] of mud, destined for destruction.”
Thus says the Lord of hosts: “As I have spoken, so it will happen; as I have planned, so it will stand.
I will destroy the Persians from my land and from my borders. They will trample them down, their yoke will be removed from them, and their burden will be lifted from their shoulders.”
This is the plan that the Lord has devised against the whole world, and this is his hand raised over all the nations.
Who can turn back the plan of the holy Lord? Who can restrain his uplifted hand?
This message came in the year when King Ahaz died.
Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, because the yoke of your power has been broken.
The poor will graze within it, and needy people will rest in peace. Famine will destroy your descendants and put an end to those who remain of you.
Wail, gates of the cities! Let the terrified cities and all the Philistines cry out! For smoke has come from the south, and then they will no longer remain.
And what will the kings of the nations say? “Look, the Lord has founded Zion, and because of this the humble among the people will be saved.”
In the night they will destroy Moab, and in the night they will plunder Moab’s wealth.
Mourn for yourselves, because Dibon has been destroyed, where your idol dwells and where your sacrifices are.
Put on sackcloth in her streets, weep on her rooftops, and cry out in her squares as you weep.
For Heshbon cried out and called as far as Jahaz, and their voice was heard.
Moab’s heart cries out alone as far as Zoar, for she is a three-year-old heifer. On the ascent of Luhith they weep to you and go up the road to Horonaim.
And the waters of Nimrim will dry up, and its grass will perish; no greenery will be found within it.
Even so, you will not escape, for I will bring Arabs into the lowlands, and they will seize it.
For her wailing has joined with that in the regions of Moab, at Eglaim, and they cried out as far as the pool of Elim.
The waters of Rimmon will be filled with blood, for I will bring Arabs against Rimmon. I will remove the descendants of Moab, Ariel, and those who remain of Admah.
I will send them like wild animals into a rocky land.
For you have become like a bird that drove her young away and abandoned them. You, daughter of Moab, have become like a fattened lamb.
Arnon deliberates at length about making herself a shelter where she can live in hiding and [?]. Day and night they are terrified and tremble.

Do not settle beside you those who have fled from Moab, so that they may be your protection against those who pursue you; for the killers have perished, and the messenger over all the earth has been destroyed.
His throne will be established through mercy, and he will sit on it in righteousness. He will judge in the house of David, seek justice, and pursue righteousness.
We have heard of Moab's pride and excessive arrogance, and I brought in pride.
Wail, Moab, for they all cry out over Moab. Those who live in Desem will be disgraced and will not be ashamed.
The fields of Heshbon will mourn, and so will the vine of Sibmah.
Therefore I weep for the vine of Sibmah as Jazer weeps.
I will remove joy and gladness from the vineyard. They will no longer rejoice in the vineyard or tread grapes in the winepress, for it has perished.
Therefore my inward parts tremble like a harp because of Moab, and my bones are like a wall they have built.
It will bring you shame, because Moab has labored for her idol and goes to her gods to pray, but they cannot save her.
This is the word that the Lord spoke concerning Moab, which he spoke long ago.

And now I say: Within three years, counted as a hired worker's years, Moab's glory will be disgraced, along with all her great wealth. Not even a little will remain, and she will no longer recover her glory.
Look, Damascus will disappear from among the cities and will fall.
She will be plundered forever and will then rest among shepherds' dwellings, with no one to frighten her.

Ephraim has no fortress in which to take refuge. No king will reign any longer in Damascus. As for those who remain of Syria, you are no better than the people of Israel and their glory. This is what the Lord of hosts says.
At that time Jacob's glory will perish, and his abundant flesh will grow thin.
It will be like someone gathering a ripe harvest and reaping grain and ears of corn. It will be like someone gathering ripe ears of corn in the valleys.
Gleanings will remain in it, like two or perhaps three olives at the top of a tall tree, with perhaps four or five remaining among its branches. This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says.
On that day a person will trust in his Maker, and his eyes will look toward the Holy One of Israel.
They will no longer trust in their idols or in the work of their hands, which their fingers made, and they will not cut wood for their unclean idols.
At that time your cities will be laid waste like the devastation of the Amorites and Hivites before the people of Israel, and they will become a wilderness.
For you have abandoned your God and Savior, and you have not remembered the Lord who reminded you, the Lord who appeared to you. Therefore you will plant a false planting and sow a seed of shame.

And when you plant, you will go wrong, and what you sowed will bear fruit in the morning, at harvest, on the day you pass on your inheritance. And like a father to his son, you too will pass on an inheritance to your children.
Woe to the many nations who have swollen like the waves of the sea; in the same way you are tossed about. And [?] many peoples roar like water.

The multitude of people is like abundant water, like a great torrent of water descending forcefully from [?]. They will destroy it and come down from far away, like straw dust before a whirlwind that sweeps it away, and like the dust of a chariot that the wind carries off.
Toward evening they will lament; before morning comes, it will be no more for them.
Woe to the land of ships that have wings, among the rivers of Ethiopia!
They will send a ship out to sea and letters across the water.
And they will remain on their journeys.
For this is what the Lord said to me: My city will stand firm like the light at noon and like a rain cloud in the days of the rainy season.
Before the harvest, when the blossom has faded, the unripe grape will bear sour fruit.
The birds of the sky and the wild animals will gather over it.
At that time a lowly and shaven people, and those from a great nation, will bring an offering to the Lord of hosts, from now and forever.
Look, the Lord rides on a swift cloud and comes into Egypt. The works of the Egyptians’ hands will shake before his face, and their hearts will tremble within them.
Egyptians will rise against Egyptians. A man will kill his brother, and a man his neighbor; city will fight against city, and law against law.

The Egyptians’ spirits will be terrified within them, and I will overturn their plans. They will consult their gods and their idols, those who speak from beneath the earth, and those who use incantations.
I will hand the Egyptians over to people who will enslave them cruelly, and to kings who will rule them harshly. This is what the Lord of hosts says.
The Egyptians will drink water near the sea, because the river will dwindle and dry up.
Every place where streams of water stand will dry up, along with every thicket of reeds and rushes.
All the green grass beside the river, and everything sown along the riverbank, will dry up and disappear.
And the fishermen will mourn, and all who lower their fishing gear into the river will weep. Those who spread their nets and the fishermen will lament.
Those who repair torn nets will be ashamed, as will those who make [?].
And those who work at it will suffer, and all who work with the equipment will [?], and their souls will suffer.
The messengers of Tanis will become foolish, and the counsel of the wise men and the kings’ advisers will go astray.
Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you, then; let them explain to you what the Lord has planned against Egypt.
The messengers of Tanis have come to an end, and the messengers of Memphis have risen up. The Egyptians have gone astray, people by people.
For the Lord has sent a demon of deception, and the Egyptians have gone astray in everything they do, like a drunkard staggering, like someone whom blood has sent reeling.
No work will be found for Egypt that has a head or a tail, a beginning or an end.
At that time the Egyptians will be like women, afraid and trembling before the face of the Lord of hosts, because of what he brings down upon them.
The land of Judah will become a source of dismay to the Egyptians.
At that time five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan, and the cities will unite in the name of the Lord, the Lord of mighty ones.
At that time there will be an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt, and a house of the Lord within their borders.

And it will be a sign for the Lord in the land of Egypt forever. For they will cry out to the Lord because of those who oppress them, and he will send them a man who will save them. He will judge him and save him.
Egypt will become a sign for the Lord.
The Lord will strike them with a plague and restore them to life. Afterward they will return to the Lord, and he will hear them and have mercy on them.
At that time there will be a road from Egypt to the road of Persia. The Persians will travel to Egypt, and the Egyptians will enter Persia, and the Egyptians will serve the Persians.
At that time Israel will be a third alongside Egypt and Persia, and they will be blessed on the earth.
The Lord of hosts has blessed them, saying, “Blessed are my people in Egypt and those in Persia, and Israel, my inheritance.”
In the year when the Tartan came to Ashdod, when Arna, king of Persia, sent him, he attacked Ashdod and captured it.

At that time the Lord spoke to Isaiah son of Amoz and said to him, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and loosen your sandals from your feet. Walk naked and barefoot.” He did so and walked naked and barefoot.
The Lord said, “Just as my servant Isaiah walked naked and barefoot, so he will be a sign and a wonder for three years to both Egypt and Ethiopia.
In the same way the king of Persia will carry away the Egyptians and Ethiopians. They will take their young and old captive, naked and barefoot, and Egypt’s shame will be exposed.
Egypt will be defeated along with Ethiopia, and Egypt will be put to shame along with those they trusted and boasted about.”
At that time those who live on this island will say, “Look, we trusted them to save us, and we sought refuge with them.”
Like a storm from the wilderness, it passed through the desert and came from a fearsome land.
The one who showed me a terrible vision told me about it.
Because of this my waist is racked with pain, and agony has seized me like a woman giving birth.
My heart went astray, my sin overwhelmed me, and my soul was terrified.
Set the table; eat and drink.
For this is what the Lord said to me: “Go quickly, send watchmen, and report what you have heard.”
I saw two horsemen riding: one was riding a donkey and the other was riding a camel.
He called Uriah the watchman.
A rider came along the road and answered me, saying, “Babylon has fallen, and all its idols and the works of its hands have been smashed to the ground.”
Listen, you who remain and you who suffer. Listen to what I heard from the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, who told it to me.
Call them to me from Seir. Guard the watchposts.
Keep watch day and night.
You will spend the night in the forest on the road to Dedan.
Bring water to those who are thirsty, you who live in the land of Teman. Bring food and welcome those who have fled.
From the many who were killed, and from the many who fled, and from the many warriors, and from the many archers with their bows drawn, and because of the many who fell in battle.
For this is what the Lord said to me: Within a year, reckoned as a hired worker's year, the glory of the descendants of Kedar will come to an end.
The remaining archers and mighty men among the descendants of Kedar will perish, says the Lord, the God of Israel.
What has happened to you now, that you have all gone up onto the rooftops for nothing?
The city is full of cries. Your slain were not killed in war, and those of yours who perished did not perish in battle.
All your messengers fled. Those who were taken captive were tormented with chains, and your mighty men fled far away.
Therefore leave me to weep bitterly. Do not keep trying to comfort me over the destruction of the daughter of my people.
For it is a day of turmoil, destruction, trampling, and breaking, from the Lord of hosts.
The men of Elam took up quivers, along with men riding horses and an army drawn up for battle.
Chariots will fill your valleys, and horses will block your gates.
They will open the gates of Judah.
They will see how numerous they have become and how the water of the old city's pools has been diverted.
They also tore down the houses of Jerusalem and the fortification that protected the city.
You brought out water for yourselves between the two walls that are in the old pool. But you did not look to the one who created it long ago, nor did you acknowledge the one who made it.
On that day the Lord of hosts brought weeping and mourning, sackcloth and shaved heads.
But they held a festival with joy and rejoicing, and slaughtered cattle and sheep.
This word was heard in the ears of the Lord of hosts: “This sin of yours will not be forgiven you until you die.”
This is what the Lord of hosts says: “Go to the house of Shebna, the treasurer, and say to him:
“Why have you come here, and what business do you have here? You are making yourself a tomb; you have carved yourself a memorial in the rock on the cliff and made yourself a house.
Look, the Lord of hosts will strip you of your clothing and the crown of your glory.
He will throw you into a vast, boundless land, and there you will die. He will disgrace your splendid chariot, and they will trample your master's house.
You will be removed from your office and from your authority.
At that time I will call my servant Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah.

I will dress him in your clothing and give him your crown. I will entrust him with your administration and give him your authority. I will transfer everything in your hands into his hands. He will be a father to those who live in Jerusalem and those who live in Judah.

I will give him the glory of David. He will rule, and no one will refuse his rule. I will place the keys of the house of David on his shoulders. If he opens, no one will shut; and if he shuts, no one will open.
He will appoint him governor of a secure land, and I will seat him on the glorious throne of his father's house.
Every honored person in his father's house, both small and great, will rely on him, and on that day they will hang upon him.

This is what the Lord of hosts says: “The man who stands in a secure place will be shaken. They will take him away, and he will fall, and his glory will perish from him, for the Lord has spoken thus.”
Let the ships of Chalcedon wail, for it has been destroyed. They no longer come from the land of Kittim, and they will take them captive.
What are the island's inhabitants like—the foreign settlers from Phoenicia who crossed the sea's mighty waters?
Like seed traded at harvest are the foreign peoples who came in.
“Be ashamed, Sidon,” said the sea. The strength of the sea said, “I have not been in labor or given birth; I have not raised young men or brought up young women.”
For as soon as it is heard in Egypt, the anguish of Tyre will seize them.
Go to Chalcedon, and let those who live on the island wail for her.
Was this not your pride from ancient times, before they gathered her up?
Who planned this against Tyre? Is she not superior, and is she not powerful? Her merchants are honored princes of the earth.
The Lord of hosts has planned to overthrow all the pride of the honored and to disgrace all the great ones of the earth.
Cultivate your land, for ships will no longer come from Chalcedon.
Your hand toward the sea, which provoked kings, will now grow weak.
They will say, “Do not do it again, and do not oppress the daughter of Zion. Even if you go to the land of Kittim, you will find no rest there either.”
For the Persians have devastated even the land of the Chaldeans, and its foundations have fallen.
Wail, ships of [?], for your stronghold has been shattered.
At that time Tyre will remain for seventy years, as long as the days of a king and as long as the days of a human being. After [?] years, Tyre will be like the song of a prostitute.
Take a lyre and go around the city, you forgotten prostitute. Play skillfully and sing many songs so that they will remember you.
After seventy years the Lord will visit Tyre, and she will return again to her former state. She will become a trading place for all the kings of the world on the face of the earth.

Her trade and her earnings will be holy to the Lord. They will not be for those who gather, but for those who dwell before the Lord. All her business will provide food and drink and satisfaction, and her memorial will bring satisfaction before the Lord.
Look, the Lord will devastate the world and plunder it. He will lay bare its face and scatter those who live in it.

The people will be like the priest, the slave like his master, the female slave like her mistress, the buyer like the seller, the borrower like the lender, and the one who collects payment like the debtor.
Look, the earth will be utterly devastated, and the earth will be thoroughly plundered, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
The earth has mourned and been devastated, and the world has been ruined. The great ones of the earth have mourned.
For the earth has sinned along with those who live in it, because they have transgressed the law, altered the ordinance, and rejected the everlasting covenant.
Therefore the earth will swallow them up, because those who live in it have sinned.
Let the wine and the vineyard mourn, and let all who rejoice in their hearts weep.
The joy of their drums has ceased. The revelry and wealth of sinners have ceased. The sound of the lyre has ceased.
They have been put to shame and do not drink wine. Mead has become bitter to those who drink it.
All the cities have been plundered, and the houses have been shut so that no one can enter them.
Weep over the wine, for all the joy of the earth has been brought to an end.
The cities will be left plundered, and the houses will be stripped, abandoned, and destroyed.
All this will happen in the land, among the nations.
But those who remain on the earth will rejoice together in the glory of the Lord. The waters of the sea will be stirred up.
Therefore the glory of the Lord will be in the islands of the sea; the name of the Lord will be praised.
O Lord, God of Israel, from the ends of the earth we have heard of his wonderful promise to the righteous.
Fear, a pit, and a snare are upon those who live on the earth.
Whoever flees from fear will fall into the pit, and whoever comes out of the pit will be caught in the snare.
The earth will tremble and be shaken, and the earth will be brought low.
It will stagger like a drunkard and like [?] from wine; it will shake and sway like a grain watchman's hut. It will fall and be unable to rise, because its sin weighs heavily upon it.
At that time the Lord will bring his hand upon the heavenly host and upon the kings of the earth.
They will be gathered together, shut up, kept under guard, and bound, and he will confine them for many generations.
Their multitude will melt away, and their defenses will fall, for the Lord, who has power, will reign in Zion and Jerusalem and will be glorified before the elders.
O Lord my God, I will praise you and proclaim your name, because you have done a wonderful deed, and your counsel from long ago has proved faithful.
For you have reduced cities to earth, and he has brought down fortified cities, the foundation of sinners; their cities will never be rebuilt.
Because of this, poor people will bless you, and the cities of oppressed people will bless you.

For you have become a helper to all the poor cities. You have sheltered those who grieve in their distress; you have delivered them from evil people. You have sheltered the thirsty and the souls of oppressed people.
Like the souls of fainthearted people who thirsted in Zion because of sinful people to whom you handed us over.
The Lord of hosts will arrange for all the nations to drink joy and drink wine on this mountain.
They will anoint themselves with perfume on this mountain.

Death was swallowed up, and he prevailed. And again the Lord God removed every tear from every face, and he removed the people's disgrace from all the earth, because the Lord spoke with his own mouth.
At that time they will say, “Here is the Lord our God, in whom we have trusted, and he will save us.”
The Lord will give us rest on this mountain, and they will trample Moab as grain is trampled with wheels.
He will raise his hand against him, just as he inflicted pain and killed; and he humbled the insolence of the one who raised his hand against him.
He will bring down the height of the walls of your fortress, and it will be lowered to the ground.
At that time they will sing this song in Judah and say, “Here is a strong city, our salvation, which provides walls and defenses.”
Open the gates so that the people who keep righteousness and embrace uprightness may enter.
He will seek refuge in peace forever. We have trusted in you.
O Lord, great and eternal God,
you have humbled and brought down those who dwell on high. You will demolish fortified cities and bring them down to the ground.
The feet of the meek and the humble will trample them.
There will be a straight path for the righteous, and the path of the upright will be clear.
For the path of the Lord is straight.
At night my spirit goes out to you, O Lord my God, for your commandment is a light upon the earth.
For the sinner who does not learn righteousness on earth and does not do good has come to an end.
Lord, they do not recognize your uplifted arm, but when they recognize it, they will be ashamed.
Lord our God, give us peace, for you have given us everything.
Lord our God, take possession of us. Lord, we know no other besides you, and we invoke your name.
The dead will not see life, and practitioners of sorcery will raise them.
Add misfortune to them, Lord; add misfortune to the honored people of the earth.
Lord, in our suffering we remembered you, and with a little suffering you disciplined us.
As a woman in labor, nearing childbirth, cries out in her pain, so it was with your beloved.
Because of our fear of you, Lord, we conceived, suffered labor pains, and gave birth to the spirit of your salvation on earth.
The dead will rise, and those in the tombs will live, and those in the earth will rejoice.
Go, my people, enter your house, shut your door, and hide for a little while, until the Lord’s wrath passes.
Look, the Lord will bring punishment from his sanctuary [?] upon those who live on the earth. The earth will reveal its blood and will no longer cover the slain.

On that day the Lord will bring a holy, great, and mighty sword against the serpent and against the dragon that runs toward the serpent and the dragon that does evil. He will kill the serpent that is in the sea.
On that day, a good and beloved vineyard, which has belonged to her since long ago.
I am a strong city. They attack a single city, and I have watered it in vain. At night it will be besieged, and by day its wall [?] will fall, and there is no one to raise it.
Who will appoint me to guard stubble in the wilderness? Because of this I fought against her [?].
Those who live within it cried out, “Let us make peace with him.”
Those who are coming are the descendants of Jacob, for Jacob and Israel will sprout and bear fruit, and his fruit will fill the world.
Yet he will not be struck as he struck; and as he killed, so he will be killed.
With strife and reproach he will send them away.
Because of this, Jacob’s sin will be removed, and this is his blessing when I take away his sin: when they make all their stones cut to pieces like finely crushed gypsum.
They will strip the dwelling of the grazing animals like a pasture they have abandoned. [?] will graze by day and rest there.
And [?] will dry up, and no greenery at all will be found within it.
At that time the Lord will close off the area from the river's channel to Rhinocorura.
On that day they will blow a great horn, and those who were lost in the land of Persia and those who were lost in Egypt will come and worship the Lord on his holy mountain in Jerusalem.
Woe to the crown of shame of Ephraim’s hired men! A flower falling from his inheritance, on the summit of a fertile mountain—those who get drunk without wine.

Look, the Lord’s scourge is strong and terrifying, like hail falling where there is no roof. It comes down powerfully like abundant, overflowing water that rushes along, and it brings rest to the earth and the land.
With their feet and their hands they will trample the crown of pride of Ephraim’s hired men.
The flower that falls from the confidence of their glory on the summit of the high mountain will be like an early fig: whoever sees it runs to it and wants to swallow it before taking it in his hand.
On that day the Lord of hosts will be a woven crown of glory for the [?], the people who remain.
By a spirit of judgment, by justice, and by the power of God, they will cleanse their throats.

For these people became drunk on wine, and mead led them astray. Mead bewildered the priest and the prophet, and wine overwhelmed them. They went astray in drunkenness, and this is a deception of the eyes.
So this plan they devised will be swallowed up—their plan to oppress the poor.
To whom have we announced evil, and to whom have we announced news? To those taken away from sucking the breast and prevented from drinking milk.
Receive suffering upon suffering, and expect hope upon hope; a little more, and a little more.
With sinful lips and in another language they will speak to this people.
They will say to them, “This is the rest of the one who drinks, and this is his crushing.” But they refused to listen.
The word of God will become for them suffering upon suffering and hope upon hope, a little more and a little more, so that they may go and fall backward, be broken, be trapped, and be captured.
Therefore hear the word of God, you afflicted men and messengers of the people of Jerusalem.
For you say, “We have sworn an oath with Sheol and made an agreement with death, so that the storm will not reach us or find us, even if it passes through.”

Therefore this is what the Lord God said: “Look, I am laying a stone in Zion, in its foundation—a chosen and honored cornerstone of great value, around its foundation. Whoever believes in it will not be put to shame.
I will establish hope in righteousness, and my mercy in balance. Those who trust in emptiness and falsehood will not escape the storm.”
Your oath with death will be annulled, and your covenant with Sheol will not stand.
As soon as it comes, it will sweep you away. Every morning your day will draw near to you, and at night there will be an expectation of evil.
We cannot [?] or depart; we ourselves have labored to gather you together.
The Lord will rise like a rock of sinners and will be in the valley of Gibeon. He will do his work in wrath—a bitter work. He will make his wrath astonishing, and his fury extraordinary.
Do not rejoice, and do not let your fortification grow strong, for I have heard from the Lord of Hosts of a destruction and a cutting short that he will carry out throughout the earth.
Hear my voice and listen to me; pay attention and hear my words.
Does the plowman plow all the time? Does he begin sowing before he has plowed his land?
Does he not, after leveling his field, sow a little black cumin and cumin, and then sow wheat and barley?
The earth will be taught by the judgment of God and will rejoice.
For black cumin is not threshed by force, nor is cumin crushed with a cartwheel. Cumin is beaten with a rod, and black cumin is eaten with grain.
I too will not torment you forever, nor will the word of my bitterness trample you.
This that has come from the Lord of Hosts is wonderful; but you wish to magnify empty foolishness.
Woe to Ariel, the city against which David fought!
For I will afflict Ariel, and this will be my strength and my wealth.
I will surround you as David did, besiege you, and set a rampart around you.
Your speech will sink into the earth, and your voice will be like that of someone speaking from beneath the earth. You will grow weak and lower your voice into the earth.
The wealth of sinners will be like dust from [?] and like chaff carried by the wind. At that time it will come suddenly from the Lord of hosts.
For he will come with thunder, shaking, a great noise, an approaching storm, and a flame of consuming fire.

The wealth of all the nations will be like someone dreaming a dream—all those who wage war against Israel, all those who wage war against Jerusalem, and all those who have gathered against it and besieged it.

They will be like those who eat and drink in their dreams, but when they wake, their dreams have deceived them; and like a thirsty person who dreams of drinking water, but wakes still thirsty, having hoped in vain. Such will be the wealth of all the nations that have waged war against Mount Zion.
Grow weak and be dazed; become drunk, but not on mead or wine.
For the Lord has made them drink an evil spirit that dazes them and covers their eyes—the eyes of their prophets and their messengers who see hidden things.
All these words will be to you like the words of a sealed book. They will give the book to a man who knows how to read and say to him, “Read this.”
They will give the book to a man who cannot read and tell him, “Read this.”
The Lord said, “This people draws near to me with their mouths and honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.”
Therefore, look, I will once again remove this people. I will remove them, destroy the wisdom of their wise men, and hide the counsel of their counselors.
Woe to those who devise deep plans without the Lord!
Are you not like a potter’s clay? Will a work of art say to its craftsman, “You did not make us”? Or will a work say to its maker, “You did not do well in making me”?
Will it not be only a little while before Lebanon becomes like Mount Carmel and Carmel becomes like a forest?
On that day the deaf, as well as those in darkness and those in gloom, will hear the words of a book.
The poor will rejoice gladly in the Lord, and the destitute will be filled with joy in the Holy One of Israel.
For the sinner has come to an end, the arrogant one has perished, and those who act unjustly in wickedness have been destroyed.
And those who lead people astray with words, and all who argue at the gates, bring a snare; they have turned the righteous aside through their injustice.
Therefore this is what the Lord said to the house of Jacob, whom he brought out of the house of Abraham: “Jacob will not now be ashamed, and your face will not now change.”
When their children see my works, they will sanctify my name for my sake. They will sanctify the house of Jacob and fear the God of Israel.
Those who went astray in their spirit will know wisdom, and those who grumble will learn commandments, and a foul tongue will learn to speak peace.
Woe to the children of the rebellious! This is what the Lord said: “You have made plans, but not through me, and you have made arrangements, but not through my Spirit, so that you add sin upon sin.”
You who travel down to the land of Egypt without asking me, to receive help from Egypt and Pharaoh!
Pharaoh will be a shield of shame for you, and those in whom you have trusted in Egypt will become a disgrace.
The messengers of Tanis are wicked envoys.
They labor in vain among nations that will be of no help to them, but only bring shame and disgrace.

In suffering and distress are the lion and the lion’s cub, and from there come flying beasts of the earth. People load their wealth on camels and donkeys and carry it to nations that will be of no help to them, but only bring shame and disgrace.
Egypt will be of no use to you. Tell them that what they have advised is useless.
Now sit down and write this on a tablet, so that it may remain throughout its lifetime and forever.
For they are a rebellious people, lying children who refused to hear the law of the Lord.
They say to the prophets, “Do not report to us,” and to those who see visions, “Do not tell us. But what will you tell us? Make another deception known to us.”
Turn us away from this road, let us leave this path, and remove the teaching of Israel from us.
Therefore the Holy One of Israel says this: Because you have rejected this word, trusted in falsehood, grumbled, and put your confidence in this matter,
therefore this sin of yours will be like a collapsing wall of a fortified city, which falls suddenly when its time comes.
Its fall will be like the shattering of an earthenware vessel. Its fragments will be crushed so fine that among them no shard will be found with which to take up fire or scoop up a little water.
The Lord, the Holy One of Israel, says this: When you repent and weep, you will live and know where you are; for you have trusted in emptiness, and your strength will become worthless.
You say, “We will escape on our horses.” Therefore you will flee. You say, “We will ride swift horses.” Therefore those who pursue you will be swift.
A thousand will be terrified at the voice of one, and at the voice of five many will flee, until you are left like scorched straw.
And again the Lord will show you kindness. Therefore he has risen up to have mercy on you, for the Lord our God is a judge.
For a holy people will dwell in Jerusalem, in Zion.
The Lord will give you your food in suffering and your water in distress. Then the one who leads you astray will no longer approach, and your eyes will look upon those who led you astray.
Your ears will hear behind you the voice of those who went astray, saying, “Let us walk on this road,” whether to the right or to the left.

And [?] the idols plated with silver and adorned with gold. You will reduce them to fine dust and [?], and pour it out like the water of a woman sitting in menstruation; and like excrement you will throw it inside them.
At that time he will send rain for the seed of your land. The harvest of grain from your land will be abundant, and your grazing animals will grow fat and graze in a broad, grassy land.
Your oxen and your donkeys that work the land will eat straw mixed with barley.
On every tall mountain and every high hill, water will flow at that time, when many perish and the tower falls.
The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold at that time, when the Lord heals the wound of his people and cures the pain of your scourging.
Look, the name of the Lord comes after a long time, and his anger burns. The sound of his lips comes with glory, and his voice is full of anger; the scourge of his wrath consumes like fire.

His breath flows like water in a ravine, reaching up to the neck. It divides to trouble the nations and lead them astray into futility. Error will pursue them, seize them, and take vengeance on them to their faces.
You will sing and rejoice and enter my sanctuary, continually celebrating a festival. Like joyful people, you will enter with a lyre into the mountain of the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.

The Lord will make his glorious voice heard and show the wrath of his arm and the scourge of his anger. He will burn with consuming fire and with a violent storm, like heavy rain and great hailstones falling.
At the voice of the Lord, the Persians will be defeated by the scourge with which he strikes them.
Those whom he hoped would help him, and those in whom he trusted, will hold him back.
For they were not those whom he had considered beforehand.
Woe to those who go down to the land of Egypt for help and trust in their horses and their chariots, because their horses are plentiful and their numbers are very great.
Yet he is wise; he has brought disaster upon them and will not take back his word. He will rise against the house of wicked men and against their worthless source of confidence.
The Egyptians are merely human beings and not God; a horse is flesh and not help. The Lord will bring his hand upon them, and those who helped them will grow weak, and they will all perish together.

For this is what the Lord said to me: As a lion and a young lion roar over their prey and cry out over it until their voice fills the mountains, and they are overcome and terrified by the greatness of its fury, so the Lord of hosts will come down to fight on Mount Zion, among its mountains.
Like a bird flying, so the Lord of hosts will fight for Jerusalem. He will help and save, rescue and preserve life.
Turn back, you who devise deep schemes in order to rebel.
For on that day people will reject their gods of gold and silver, which they made with their own hands.
The Assyrians will fall, but not by a human sword. It is not a man's blade that will devour them, and it is not from a sword that they will flee.
A rock will swallow them, and they will be overcome. Even the one who escapes will be captured.
For look, a righteous king will reign, and rulers will judge with righteousness.
A man will conceal his words and hide himself like someone sinking into the deep. His glory will appear in Zion like a flowing river in a thirsty land.
Then they will no longer trust in human beings, but they will listen attentively with their ears.
A weak heart will hear and understand, and a foul tongue will quickly learn to speak peace.
They will no longer appoint a fool to be a ruler, and your servant will no longer say to you, “Be silent.”
For a fool speaks foolishness, and his heart thinks empty thoughts, so that he acts unjustly and speaks sinfully against the Lord, scatters the hungry person, and strips the thirsty person bare.
For the minds of the wicked devise injustice, to kill the needy with their unjust words and overturn justice for the poor.
But the righteous offer wise counsel, and that counsel will endure.
Wealthy women, rise and hear my voice. Confident daughters, listen attentively to my words.
Each year, commemorate the day of suffering that you anticipate.
Be terrified and mourn, you who feel secure. Strip yourselves and be laid bare; bind your waists.
Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields and for the fruitful vineyard.
For the beloved land of my people, thorns and thistles will grow in their fields, and joy will be removed from all their houses. The wealthy city will be plundered.
Her houses. They will abandon the wealth of their cities and the inheritance of their houses. Their cities will remain in misery forever, a delight for wild donkeys and a pasture for animals.
Until a spirit comes upon you from on high.
His justice will rest in the wilderness, and his righteousness will dwell in Carmel.
There will be peace and the work of righteousness. Righteousness will occupy a resting place, and they will trust in it forever.
The people will live in a city of peace, dwell securely, and rest in prosperity.
Even if hail falls, it will not reach you.
Blessed are those who sow where there is water and where the ox and donkey walk.
Woe to those who dishonor you, yet there is no one who dishonors you. And whoever betrayed you—it was not you whom he betrayed.
Lord, have mercy on us, for we have put our trust in you.
At the majesty of his voice the nations were terrified; in fear of you the nations were scattered.
And now, look, your spoils, small and great, are being gathered. As someone gathers locusts, so they will mock you.
Holy is the Lord who dwells on high, and Zion is filled with righteousness and justice.
And they will bring them lawfully into the treasuries of our salvation.
Look, those whom you formerly feared now fear you because of your majesty, and they tremble before you. Messengers are sent out, weeping bitterly and asking for peace.
For their roads have fallen into ruin, and the majesty of the nations has passed away. Their covenant has been broken, and you do not regard them as human beings.
The earth has become desolate, and Lebanon has been put to shame. Sharon has become a thicket.
“Look, now I will arise,” says the Lord. “Now I will be glorified, and now I will be exalted.
Now you will see, and now you will be astonished. The strength of your breath will come to nothing, and fire will consume you.”
The nations will be like burning thorns in the wilderness, burned and cast away.
Those far away will hear what I have done, and those nearby will know my power.
Those in Zion have rebelled against me and wronged me. Look, trembling will seize the sinners.

The one who walks in righteousness and speaks uprightly, who hates the way of injustice, who hates sin and wrongdoing, who withdraws his hands from bribes, who turns away his ears so as not to hear a death sentence, and who closes his eyes so as not to see oppression—
such a person will live on high, in a cave in a strong rock. Food and water will be given to him in righteousness.
You will see the king in glory, and your eyes will see a distant land.
And your soul will reflect on fear.

The small and the great among the people, who have not taken counsel and who do not understand profound speech, so that they do not hear an unjust people; and whoever hears is like someone without understanding.

Look, Zion, the city of our salvation! With your own eyes you will see Jerusalem, a prosperous city. Its houses will not shake, the stakes of its tent will never be moved, and its ropes will not be broken.
For the name of the Lord is great among you. In your land there will be rivers and streams of water, broad and spacious. You will not travel this route, nor will ships travel it.
For the Lord my God is great, and he will not pass me by. The Lord is our judge, the Lord is our God, and the Lord is our king. He, the Lord, will save us.
Your ropes have broken because they were not straight. Your mast has rotted, and your sail has not extended. It will not raise a signal until they seize it and plunder it.
