The people living among them will not say, “I am weary,” for their sins will be forgiven.
Gather, people, and listen, angels. Let the earth and those in it listen, and the world and all the nations in it.
For the Lord’s wrath is against all nations, and his scourge is upon all their multitude, to destroy them and hand them over to war.
The bodies of their slain will be cast out, and their stench will rise. The mountains will be soaked with their blood.
The sky will be rolled up like a scroll, and all the stars will fall like vine leaves and like leaves falling from a fig tree.
My sword has become drunk in heaven. Look, it burns against Edom and descends in judgment upon a people doomed to destruction.
The Lord’s sword is filled with blood and laden with the fat of sheep, goats, and rams. For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in Edom.
The mighty will fall with them, along with [?] and bulls. The earth will become drunk with their blood and drenched with their fat.
For it is the day of the Lord’s judgment, and the year of repayment for Zion’s judgment.
Her streams will turn into pitch, and her land will become sulfur; her land will burn.
Day and night, like pitch, it will never go out. Its smoke will rise upward. It will lie waste from generation to generation, and remain ruined for many days.
Birds, [?], hedgehogs, and [?] will dwell within her.
Her messengers will perish, and her kings and princes will be destroyed.
Thorn trees will grow in her cities and fortresses. She will become a city of demons and a dwelling place for ostriches.
Demons and [?] will meet there, and they will all cry out there. There, [?] with cattle’s hooves will dwell and find a resting place for themselves.
Hedgehogs will breed there, and the earth will keep its young safe. Deer will meet there and see one another face to face.
They will pass by according to their number, and not one of them will be lost. They will not search for one another, because the Lord has commanded them.
He will give them their allotted share; his hand has given it to them as an inheritance, and they will graze there. They will inherit it forever, generation after generation, and rest in it.
Let the thirsty wilderness rejoice; let the desert be glad and blossom like a flower.
The plain of the Jordan will blossom and rejoice. The glory of Lebanon has been given to it, and the glory of Carmel. My people will see my glory, and they will exalt the Lord.
Grow strong, weak hands and lame feet.
Encourage your feeble hearts: be strong and do not be afraid.
At that time the eyes of the blind will regain sight, and the deaf will hear.
At that time the lame will run like deer, and the tongues of the mute will speak clearly. For water has sprung up in the wilderness and flowed through the thirsty land.
Trees will grow in the wilderness and spring up in the thirsty land. There, where the birds dwell, will be a place of [?] and trees.
It will be called a pure road and a holy road. No unclean person will pass along it, and there will be no unclean road there. Those who were scattered will walk on it and will not go astray.
There will be no lion there, nor will any vicious beast go up onto it or be found there. But those who have been rescued will walk on it.

Those who have been gathered because of the Lord will return along it. They will enter Zion with rejoicing and everlasting gladness, with glory upon their heads. Joy and gladness will come to them, for pain, sorrow, and mourning have disappeared.
In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Persia came up against the fortified cities of Judah, captured them, and brought them under his control.
The king of Persia sent the Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large army.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward, Shebna the scribe, and Joakim son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him.
The Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: This is what the great king of Persia says: Whom do you trust?
Will war be won by your counsel and the words of your lips? Now, whom have you trusted, that you have rebelled against me?
Look, you have trusted in that broken reed of a staff, Egypt. If a man leans on it, a splinter will enter his hand. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
And if you say to him, ‘We have trusted in the Lord our God.’
Now come over to my master, the king of Persia, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you can bring riders for them.”
How, then, can you turn to face the rulers? All who rely on Egypt for their horses and riders are servants.
And now, have we come up into this country of yours to kill you without the Lord? For the Lord told me, ‘Go up into their country and kill them.’

Eliakim, Shebna, and Joakim said to Rabshakeh, ‘Speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew. Why are you speaking within the hearing of these people on the wall?’

Rabshakeh said to them, ‘Did my master send me to your master and to you? Was it not to these people sitting on the wall that he sent me to speak these words, so that they may eat their own dung and drink their own urine together with you?’
Then Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Hebrew, saying, ‘Hear the words of the great king, the king of Persia!’
‘This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you with words, for he cannot save you.’
‘And do not let Hezekiah tell you, “Your God will save you, and this city will not fall into the hands of the king of Persia.”’
‘Do not listen to Hezekiah.’
‘Until I come and take you to my country, a country like your own, a country of grain and wine, of wheat and vineyards.’
‘Do not let Hezekiah deceive you with words or tell you, “The Lord will save you.”’
‘Where is the god of Hamath and Arpad? And where is the god of the city of Sepharvaim? Were they able to save Samaria from my hand?’
‘Who among all the gods of the nations has saved his country from my hand, that the Lord should save Jerusalem from my hand?’
They remained silent and did not answer him a word, for the king had commanded them not to answer him a word.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward, Shebna, the army scribe, and Jehoiakim son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him what the Rabshakeh had said.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went up to the house of the Lord.
He sent Eliakim the steward, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, wearing sackcloth. They came to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, ‘This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, disgrace, and humiliation, for the woman giving birth has no strength, and labor pains have seized her.’

‘May the Lord your God hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Persia sent to mock the Lord, the living God. He has mocked him with words that the Lord your God has heard. Pray to the Lord your God for those who remain.’
King Hezekiah’s servants arrived before Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master this: ‘This is what the Lord says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the king of Persia has insulted me.’”
‘Look, I will bring a spirit upon him, and he will hear a report and return to his own country, and he will die by the sword in his own country.’
Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Persia fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had departed from Lachish.
Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, came out to fight against him. When he heard this, he turned back and sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying:
Tell King Hezekiah of Judah this: “Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, ‘Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Persia.’”
‘Have you not heard what the kings of Persia have done throughout all the regions, how they destroyed them? And will you escape?’
‘Did their gods save the nations whom my fathers killed in the land of Gozan, Resen, and Haran, on the border of Teman?’
Where are the kings of Hamath and Arpad, and of the cities of Sepharvaim, Menahe, and Gawan?
Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers and read it. He went up to the house of the Lord and spread it out before the Lord.
Hezekiah prayed to the Lord and said:
‘Lord of hosts, God of Israel, enthroned upon the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.’
Listen, Lord, and look, Lord, at the message of Sennacherib, which he sent to mock the living God.
Truly, the kings of Persia have laid waste the whole world, including their cities.
They also burned their gods with fire, because they were not gods but the work of human hands. They were wood and stone, and they destroyed them.
But you, Lord our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kings of the earth may know that you alone are the Lord.
Isaiah son of Amoz was sent to Hezekiah and said to him, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: I have heard what you prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Persia.
This is what the Lord says concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and treated you with contempt. The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
Whom have you mocked and insulted? Against whom have you raised your head? Against whom have you raised your voice? Do not lift your eyes on high and look toward the Holy One of Israel,
to mock the Lord through your messengers.
I have dammed up and drained the water and every reservoir.

Have you not heard of this, which I did long ago, which I decreed in former days? Now I have shown that I destroy the nations within their fortresses, and those who live in cities and fortify themselves.
I will bring down my hand, and they will wither. They will become like grass that withers on a rooftop, and like [?].
And now I know where you lodge, your coming in, and your going out.
The fury with which you raged, and your bitterness, have risen to me. I will put a hook in your nose and a bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back along the road by which you came.
And this is your sign.
The roots of those who remain in Judah will spread, and their growth will bear fruit above.
For from Jerusalem there will be survivors, and from Mount Zion those who escape. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.
Therefore this is what the Lord says concerning the king of Persia: He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He will not set a shield against it or besiege it.
He will return along the road by which he came, and he will not enter this city.
I will defend this city and save it for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.”
Then the angel of the Lord went out and killed 185,000 men from the Persian army. When they rose early in the morning, they found all their bodies where they had died.
Sennacherib king of Persia returned and lived in Nineveh.
While he was worshiping in the temple of Sidrach his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with a sword. They escaped to the land of Armenia.
At that time Hezekiah became ill and was near death.
Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the Lord.
He said, “Remember, Lord, how I walked before you in righteousness and with an upright heart, and did what pleased you in your sight.”
The word of the Lord came to Isaiah and said to him:
Go and tell Hezekiah: Thus says the Lord, the God of your father David: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Look, I have added fifteen years to your life.
I will rescue you from the hands of the kings of Persia, and I will defend this city.
This is the sign from the Lord that the Lord will carry out this promise.
Look, I will turn back the shadow that has descended on the ten steps of your father's house. The sun will return ten steps, and the sun will go up the ten steps down which that shadow [?] descended.
I said, "In the fullness of my days I will go to the gates of Sheol and leave behind the rest of my years."
And I said, "I will no longer see the Lord's salvation in the land of the living, and I will no longer see people."

My life among my relatives has ended, and I have lost the rest of my life. It has departed and passed away from me. Like someone who pitches his tent and takes it down, so has my life become within me, like a roll of wool that a weaver cuts off.
At that time I was troubled like a lion until morning. So my bones were crushed; it gripped me from morning until evening.
Like a swallow I chirp, and like a dove I murmur.
Lord, I spoke to you about this, and you raised up my life. I rejoiced and lived.
You had mercy on my life so that it would not perish, and you cast all my sins behind me.
For those in Sheol do not praise you, and those who die do not bless you. Those in Sheol do not hope for your mercy.
But the living bless you, as I do.
You are my Lord and my Savior, and I will not cease blessing you with song all the days of my life before the house of the Lord.
Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Take a cluster of figs, crush it, apply it to yourself, and recover."
Hezekiah said, "Is this the sign that I will go up to the house of the Lord?"
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters, envoys, and gifts to Hezekiah, because he had heard that he had been ill and near death, but had recovered.

Hezekiah was exceedingly glad because of them and showed them his treasure house: gold, silver, clothing, frankincense, precious stones, incense, all the contents of the treasury, and everything in his storehouses.

Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say to you, and where did they come from to visit you?" Hezekiah answered him, "They came to me from a distant country, from Babylon."

Isaiah said to him, "What did they see in your house?" Hezekiah answered him, "They saw everything in my house. There is nothing in my house that they did not see, including everything in my storehouses."
Isaiah said to him, “Listen now to the word of the Lord of armies.”
Look, the days are coming when everything in your house and everything your ancestors have stored up to this day will be taken and carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left for you.
Moreover, they will take your sons whom you have fathered, who have come from your own body, and make them eunuchs and servants in the palace of the king of Babylon.
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the Lord that he has spoken is good. Only let there be righteousness and peace in my days."
"Encourage my people," says the Lord.
You priests, speak to Jerusalem's heart and encourage her, for her suffering has been great. Her sin has been forgiven, and she has received from the Lord's hand double for her sins.
The voice of a herald in the wilderness: "Prepare the way of the Lord, and make straight the paths of your God."
Let every valley be filled, and every mountain and hill be brought low. Let every rough place become smooth, and let the ravines become open country.
The glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all living beings will see the Lord’s salvation, for the Lord has spoken.
A voice says, “Cry out!”
The grass withers and its fruit falls, because the spirit of the Lord speaks over it. Are not the people grass?
The grass withers and the flower falls, but the word of the Lord remains forever.
Let the one bringing good news to Zion climb a high mountain. Cry out with your strength and raise your voice, you who bring good news to Jerusalem.
And behold, the Lord!
Like a shepherd who tends his sheep, he gathers the sheep with his arm and brings joy to the pregnant ewes.
Who measured the water in his handful, and heaven with his span, and held the whole earth? Who weighed the mountains on a balance and the hills on scales?
Who has known the Lord’s mind, and who was his counselor who advised him?
With whom did he consult, and who advised him? Who showed him justice? And who showed him the way of wisdom?
All the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and like something that tips the scales. They are as nothing.
Lebanon is not enough to burn, and all the animals are not enough for sacrifice.
All the nations are as nothing, and they are regarded as though they did not exist.
To whom will you compare the Lord? Whose likeness will you say is his equal?
Is it with an image that a carpenter has made? Or with gold that a metalworker has cast? He plated it with gold, made it, and fashioned its likeness.
For a carpenter chooses wood for himself that will not rot, and with his skill he seeks a way to set up an image so that it will not wobble.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Have you not been told from the beginning? Do you not know the foundations of the earth?
He establishes the ends of the earth, and those who live in it are like locusts.
He makes rulers as though they had nothing to rule, and he made the earth out of nothing.
They will not plant or sow, and their root has not sprouted in the earth.
“And now, to whom will you compare me, so that I may be exalted?” says the holy Lord.

Lift your eyes to heaven and see who made all this: he who counts the stars and brings them out at their appointed times, and calls them all by their names, through the abundance of his glory and the strength of his power. And there is no one who has forgotten you.
Why do you say, Jacob, and why have you spoken, Israel, “My way is hidden from the Lord, and my God has gone far away from me and abandoned my cause”?
And now, do you not know, and have you not heard, that he is the eternal God? The God who created the ends of the earth does not grow hungry or tired, and no one knows his counsel.
He gives strength to the hungry and does not bring distress upon those who suffer.
Companions grow hungry, young men grow tired, and the strong stumble.
But those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength, and their wings will grow like eagles’ wings. They will run and not grow tired; they will walk and not grow hungry.
Renew yourselves before me, islands, for the strength of rulers will be renewed. Let them come forward together and speak, and let them make judgment known.
Who raised up the righteous one from the east and called him to follow in his footsteps? He brings terror before nations and kings.
He pursues them, and his feet travel the path of peace.
Who established and did this, and summoned—the one who summons from the creation of the world?
The nations at the ends of the earth saw and were afraid. They approached and came together.
Everyone urges his brother, and everyone helps his companion and speaks.
A carpenter gives strength, as does the smith who strikes with a hammer, and together they hammer them.
But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham, whom I have loved.
I took you from the ends of the earth and called you from its farthest regions. I said to you, 'You are my servant. I have chosen you and will not abandon you.'
Do not be afraid; I am with you. Be on your guard; do not let them deceive you. I am your God, who has strengthened you, helped you, and held you with my righteous right hand.
Look, all who oppose you will be ashamed and disgraced. They will become as though they had never been created, and all your enemies will perish.
You will search for the people who torment you, but you will not find them.
For I am your God, who strengthened you with my right hand and said to you:
'Do not be afraid, Jacob; you are small, Israel. I have helped you,' says the Lord who saved you, the Holy One of Israel.
Look, I have made you like the wheel of a cart that plows. You will thresh and crush mountains, grind down hills, and make them like dust.
You will winnow them, the wind will carry them away, and the storm will scatter them.
The poor who seek water and find none will rejoice, as will those whose tongues have dried up with thirst.
I will make rivers spring up among the mountains and springs bubble up in the wilderness. I will make trees grow in the desert and water flow in the thirsty land.
I will make the desert a land of cedars, box trees, myrtles, cypresses, and white poplars.
So that they may know, understand, examine, and believe that the hand of the Lord did this and the Holy One of Israel revealed it.
'Your case has drawn near,' says the Lord God. 'Your counsel has come near,' says the King of Jacob.
What will befall you has come upon you. Tell me what came before, so that we may know what you are thinking and know your outcome.
Tell us what is coming and what will happen afterward, so that we may know that you are gods. Do good and do harm, so that we may marvel at you, investigate, and know.
Where are you from, and where does your work come from? Was it not from unclean earth that they chose you?
But I have raised up the one from the south and the one from the rising of the sun, so that they may be called by my name.
Who tells of ancient things, so that we may know what came before and say, 'He is trustworthy'?
First I will give to Zion, and I will bring Jerusalem back to her path.
For there is no one among the nations or among their gods who announces anything. Even if I ask them, 'Where are they from?' they give me no answer.
Those who make them create them in vain.
Look, my servant, whom I uphold, and Israel, my chosen one, whom my soul has accepted. I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring justice to the nations.
He will not shout or cry out, and his voice will not be heard outside.
He will not break a crushed reed, and a wick that is going out [?]; rather, he will bring forth justice in righteousness.
He will shine and will not go out until he establishes justice on earth, and the nations will put their trust in his name.
This is what the Lord God says, who made heaven and established it, who made the earth firm and everything in it, who gives spirit to the peoples in it and life to those who dwell upon it.
I am the Lord God, who called you in righteousness and took hold of you with my hand. I will strengthen you and give you as an ordinance for generation after generation, as a light to the nations.
You will open the eyes of the blind and bring those who are bound out of confinement, and those who dwell in darkness out of prison.
I am the Lord God; this is my name. I will not give my glory to another or my praise to carved idols.
Look, the former things have come to pass, and I have announced new things. Look, before they are reported to you, I have told you.
Praise the Lord with a new song of praise. Let his praise come before him from the ends of the earth—you who go down into the sea and travel upon it, and the islands and those who dwell in them.
Let the wilderness and its towns rejoice.
Let them praise the Lord and tell the islands of his goodness.
The Lord God will go out as a mighty warrior. He will strike in battle and stir up zeal; he will shout against his enemies in his strength.
I have been silent since the creation of the world. Will I now remain silent forever? Will I endure like a woman giving birth [?]? I will wipe out and swallow up at the same time.
Then I will dry up mountains and hills, and I will dry up all their grass together. I will make rivers flow into islands, and I will dry up pools.
I will bring the blind along a road they do not know; I will lead them along paths they do not see. I will bring them from darkness into light, and I will level the obstacles for them.
But they turned back.
Listen, you deaf people, and look, you blind people.
Who is blind except my servants? Who is deaf except their messengers? The servants of the Lord have become blind.
You keep seeing, but do not pay attention. Your ears are open, but you do not hear.
The Lord God has resolved to justify and to magnify his glory.

I looked, and there were a people taken captive and plundered. For there are traps in houses everywhere and in the inner rooms where they have hidden them. They have plundered them, and there is no one to save them; they seize them, and there is no one to rescue them.
Who among you will pay attention to this, so that he may hear what is to come?
Who handed Jacob over to be seized, and Israel to be taken captive? Was it not the Lord, against whom they sinned? They refused to walk in his way and did not obey his law.
He brought the scourge of his wrath upon them and intensified the slaughter against them. Those who cry out around them do not understand, any of them, and they do not take it to heart.
And now, this is what the Lord God says, who made you, Jacob, and who created you, Israel: Do not be afraid, for I have saved you and called you by name.
Even if you pass through water, I am with you, and rivers will not drown you. Even if you pass through fire, the flame will not burn you.
For I am with you, your God, the Holy One of Israel, who saved you. I have appointed Egypt as your substitute, and Ethiopia and Syene as your ransom.
For you are precious in my sight, and you have been honored. I have loved you, and I will give you many people as your ransom, and angels in exchange for your life.
Do not be afraid, then, for I am with you.
And I will say to the north: Bring them.
And to all those who are called by my name: For I created them and made them for my glory.
I brought out the blind people who have eyes but do not see, and those who have ears but do not hear.
All the nations gathered together, and their messengers also gathered.
Be my witnesses, and I too will be a witness for you, says the Lord God, together with my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know, believe, and understand that I am he.
I am the Lord, and there is no other God besides me who gives life.
I declared it, I saved, and I admonished, and there was no stranger among you.
From creation, there is no one who can snatch anything from my hand; and no one can reverse what I have done.
This is what the Lord God, who saved you, the Holy One of Israel, says: Look, for your sake I will send [?] to Babylon and raise them all up; and the Persians will be bound in chains.
I am the Lord your God, the Holy One who revealed himself to Israel, your king.
This is what the Lord God says, who made a way through the sea and a passage through mighty waters.
Who brings out chariots and horses and mighty armies.
Do not remember the former things, and do not dwell on what happened long ago.
Look, I am doing something new, which is now springing up for you to recognize. I will make a way in the wilderness and make water flow in the desert.

The wild animals of the desert, the young birds, and the sirens will honor me, because I have provided water in the wilderness and made it flow in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen ones.
Whom I acquired so that they might proclaim my praise.
It is not now that I have called you, Jacob, nor have I wearied you, Israel.
For it was not to me that you sacrificed your sheep, and you did not honor me with your sacrifices. I did not make you serve me by offering sacrifices, nor did I weary you with incense.
You did not buy incense for me with gold, and I did not desire your sacrifices or the fat of your sheep. Instead, you persisted in your sins and your offenses.
I am the one who wipes out your sins and will not remember them.
But you, remember, and let us argue our case.
From the beginning, your fathers and your messengers rebelled against me.
They defiled my sanctuary, and then I commanded that they destroy Jacob and disgrace Israel.
And now listen, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
This is what the Lord God who created you says: I will help you even in the womb. Do not be afraid, Jacob, my servant, and Israel, my beloved, whom I have chosen.
For I will give water in thirst to those who travel through the wilderness, and I will place my spirit upon your offspring and my blessing upon your children.
They will sprout like grass amid the water, and like willows beside a stream of water.
One will say, “I belong to the Lord,” and another will call out in the name of Jacob. Another will write with his hand, “He belongs to the Lord,” and will call himself by the name of Israel.
This is what the Lord, the king of Israel and its savior, the God of hosts, says: I am the first and I am the last, and there is no other life-giving God besides me.
Who is a savior like me? Let him stand up and call out and declare it, and set it out before me, from the time I created humanity and forever. Let him tell you what is coming before it arrives.
Do not hide yourselves.
At that time those who fashion and carve will no longer exist. All who vainly do what their hearts desire, which does not benefit them, are worthless; they will all be put to shame.
Those who make gods and carve things that do not benefit them.
They will all dry up in the place where they were made.
For the craftsman sharpened the iron of his axe and made them. He hammered them with his hammer and strengthened them with the power of his arm. He also grows hungry and weak, and he becomes thirsty.
The chosen carpenter sets up a piece of wood according to its measure and fits it together in every part. He makes it in the likeness of a person, with a human appearance, and sets it up in a house.
That wood, which he cut from the forest, God caused to sprout and made grow tall through the rain.
A person burns it: he takes some of it and warms himself, lights a fire, and bakes bread with it. From what remains, he makes gods for himself, and they bow down to that.

He burned half of it in the fire, and with half of it he roasted meat. He ate the roast he had cooked and was satisfied. He warmed himself and said, “How pleasant this is for me! I am warm, and I have seen its fire.”
And from what remains he makes himself gods that he carves. He kneels and bows down to it, prays to it, and says to it: Save me, for you are my God.
They do not know or understand. Their eyes have been darkened so that they cannot see, and they do not understand in their hearts.

They do not reflect within themselves or recognize through their reasoning that they burned half of it in the fire and baked bread, and with [?] they roasted meat and ate it. From what remained they made an unclean thing for themselves and bowed down to it.
Know, then, that their hearts are like dirt, and they go astray. Not one of them can save himself.
Remember this, Jacob; and you, Israel, are my servant. I formed you; you are my servant, Israel. Do not forget me.
Look, I have wiped away your sins like a cloud and your offenses like mist. Return to me, and I will save you.

Let the heavens rejoice, for the Lord has had mercy on Israel. Let the foundations of the earth sound the horn. Let the mountains shout with joy, and the hills and all the forest trees within them, for the Lord has saved Jacob and has been glorified in Israel.
Thus says the Lord, who saved you and formed you in the womb: “I am the Lord, who made everything by myself. I stretched out the heavens and established the earth.”
Who else overturns the counsel of those who seek omens in a cup and those who practice divination from their own hearts? He turns the wise backward and makes their counsel foolish.

He establishes the word of his servant and confirms the counsel of his messengers. He says to Jerusalem, “You will be inhabited,” and to the cities of Judah, “You will be rebuilt, and her deserted places will sprout.”
He says to the deep, “Dry up, and let your rivers run dry.”
He says to Cyrus, “Be wise, consider, and carry out all my will.” He says to Jerusalem, “You will be rebuilt, and I will lay the foundations of my temple.”

Thus says the Lord God to my anointed, Cyrus, whom I have taken by the hand so that I may subdue nations before him and strip kings of their strength: “I will open gates before him, and cities will not be shut.”
I will go ahead of you and lower the mountains. I will break the bronze gates and shatter the iron bars.
I will give you hidden and stored-up treasures. What is unseen I will reveal to you, so that you may know that I am the Lord, who called you by your name, the God of Israel.
For the sake of my servant Jacob and Israel my chosen one, I will call you by your name and accept you.
For I am the Lord your God, and there is no other god besides me.
So that those in the east and those in the west may know that there is no other god besides me.
I formed light and made darkness. I create peace and bring calamity.
Let heaven above rejoice, and let the clouds sprinkle righteousness. Let the earth bring forth growth, and let it bring forth mercy and uprightness together. I am the Lord God who created you.

I have made you better and fashioned you like clay for a potter. Does the one who plows the ground plow all the time? Does clay say to the potter: What are you making? You cannot make anything, and you have no hands. Does clay argue with the one who molds it?
Woe to the one who says to his father, “Why did you father me?” and to his mother, “What are your labor pains for?”
For this is what the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, who made what is to come, says: “Ask me about my sons and my daughters, and command me concerning the work of my hands.”
I created the earth and humanity upon it. With my own hands I established heaven. I commanded all the stars.

I raised him up in righteousness and uprightness, and I prepared all his paths. He will build my city and bring back the captives of my people, not for a ransom and not for gifts, says the Lord of hosts.

This is what the Lord of hosts says: The labor of Egypt and the cities of Ethiopia, and the people of Seba, tall men, will come to you. They will become your servants and follow behind you with their hands bound. They will bow down to you and pray to you, for God is with you, and there is no other God besides you.
You are the Lord, and we did not know you, the God of Israel, the giver of life.
Let all who oppose him be ashamed and disgraced, and let them go away in shame.
For the Lord will save Israel with everlasting salvation. They will never be ashamed or disgraced.
This is what the Lord, who made heaven, says: He is the Lord who formed the earth and made it, and he laid it out. He did not make it in vain, but created it so that people might live in it.
I did not speak in silence, nor did I speak in a land of darkness.
Gather together and come; take counsel together, you who have escaped from the nations.

And if they speak, let them draw near so that together they may know who made this known long ago. [?] when they told you that I am the Lord, and there is no other besides me, righteous and life-giving, and there is none like me.
Turn to me and live, you who are from the ends of the earth.
I have sworn by myself: My word that has gone out of my mouth will not return.
For every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will praise the Lord.
And he will say, “Glory and righteousness will come to him.” And all who keep far from the Lord will be ashamed.
All the descendants of the children of Israel will be glorified and justified in the Lord.
Bel has fallen, and Dagon has been shattered. Their carved images have become like cattle and wild animals. Lift them up, for they are bound like a load of dung.
They have become hungry and weary, and they have no strength. They cannot save themselves from being killed, and they themselves will also be taken captive.
Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all of you who remain of Israel, who are carried from their youth and instructed from their mothers’ wombs.
Until they grow old.
To whom, then, will you compare me? Look and be wise, all of you who go astray.
You who take gold and silver out of your bags and weigh it on a scale, you hire a metalworker, and he makes for you something fashioned by human hands, and you bow down and worship them.
They carry it on their shoulders and go along. Once they have set it down, it no longer moves from its place. Even if they cry out to it, it does not hear, nor does it save itself from harm.
Remember this and weep. Repent, you who have gone astray. Turn back and turn your hearts.
And remember the things of old and the things from the creation of the world, for I am God, and there is no other besides me.
I announce the former things and what will happen afterward before it happens, and then it happens.
I call a bird from the east and from a distant land for what I have planned. I have spoken and brought it about. I have created and done it. I brought him and prepared his way.
Listen to me, you who have lost heart, who keep far from righteousness.
I have brought my righteousness near, and my salvation that comes from me will no longer delay.
Come down and sit on the ground, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit in the dust, without a throne, daughter of Persia. You will no longer be called delicate and glorious.
Take a millstone and grind flour. Remove your veil, and let your gray hair be seen. Pull up your skirts and cross the rivers.
Let your nakedness be uncovered and your disgrace be seen, for they will take righteousness away from you, and he will no longer give anyone in exchange for you.
The one who saved you—his name is the Lord of hosts, the Holy One of Israel.
Sit in shock and enter the darkness, daughter of Persia. You will no longer be called the power of a kingdom.
For you acted arrogantly against my people and defiled my inheritance.
You say, “I will rule over them forever.”
Now hear this, you pampered woman who live securely, who say in your heart, “I am the one, and there is no one like me. I will not become a widow, and my children will not die.”
Now both these things will come upon you together in a single day: you will become a widow, and your children will die.
For you trusted in your prostitution.

Destruction will come upon you, and you will not know its depth; you will fall into it. Disgrace will come upon you, and you will not be able to ward it off. Sudden death will come upon you without your knowing it.
Stand now with your sorcery and your many spells, which you learned from your youth and which do not benefit you, to see whether any can save you.

You have labored in your evil counsel. Now let those who practice divination for you stand up and save you—those who examine the heavens and look at the stars of heaven, and tell you what I will bring upon you.
Look, they will all burn like straw in a fire, and they will not save themselves from the flame. They will become burning coals for you, and you will sit beside them.
They will be your helpers. You have labored since your youth. Each person has gone astray on his own, and you have no one to save you.

Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and who came from Judah, who swear by the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, and remember him, but not in righteousness or uprightness.
You are called by the name of the holy city and rely on the God of Israel. The LORD of hosts is his name.
I announced the former things; they came from my mouth and were heard. I acted suddenly, and they came to pass.
But I knew that you are wicked, that the sinew of your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze.
I told you what was coming before it happened and made you hear it, so that you would not say, “My gods and my carved images did this to me, and my cast images commanded me.”
You have heard everything but have not understood. I have also told you of new things that will happen from now on.
And do not say: It is happening now and not long ago, and it is not what you heard in earlier days.
You did not know it or understand it, nor did I open your ear to it beforehand. I knew that you would surely betray me, for you have been called a rebel since your mother's womb.
For the sake of my name, I will [?] my wrath toward you, and I will bring my majesty upon you so that I do not destroy you.
Look, I sold you, but not for gold, and I brought you out of the furnace of poverty.
For my own sake I made you, because they defiled my name. I will not give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I called.
My hand founded the earth, and my right hand established the heavens.
Let them all gather together and listen.
I spoke, and I called. I brought him and helped him.
Come to me and hear this. Have I not spoken openly from the beginning? When it happened, I was there. Now the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit.
This is what the LORD says, who saved you and set you free, the Holy One of Israel: “I am your God, and I have shown you where to find the path you should follow.”
If only you had listened to my commandments! Your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your descendants would have been like the sand of the sea, and the offspring of your womb like the dust of the earth.
Come out of Babylon, fleeing from the Chaldeans! Proclaim a message of joy, and let it be heard; announce it to the ends of the earth.
And if they thirst for water in the wilderness, he will bring water out of a rock for them. The rock will gush for them, water will flow, and my people will drink.
But sinners will not rejoice, says the Lord.
Listen to me, islands, and pay attention to me, nations! In [?] days he will arise, says the Lord; from my mother's womb he called me by my name.
He made my mouth like a sharp razor and hid me beneath the shadow of his hand.
He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, and through you I will be glorified.”
But I said, “I have labored in vain and spent my strength on what is useless and worthless.”
And now this is what the Lord says, who formed me in my mother's womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him, and Israel too.
He said to me, “It is a great thing for you to be called my child, to restore the people of Jacob and bring back the scattered people of Israel.”
This is what the Lord who saved you, the God of Israel, says: “Honor as holy the one who afflicts his own soul, whom the nations despise, the servant of angels.”
This is what the Lord says: “On a day of favor I heard you, and on a day of salvation I helped you. I gave you as a law for the nations, to restore the land and inherit the desolate inheritance.”
You will say to the prisoners, “Come out!” And light will shine for those who are in darkness.
They will neither hunger nor thirst, and the sun's scorching heat will not hurt them. Rather, the one who has mercy on them will show them kindness and bring them to springs of water.
I will level the mountains for them, and every road will become pasture for them.
Look, some are coming from far away, some from the south and from a distant land, and some from the mountains of Persia.

Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad! Let joy burst forth from the earth and the mountains, because the Lord has shown kindness to his people and brought joy to the poor among his people.
Zion said, “Has the Lord abandoned me? Has the Lord forgotten me?”
Can a woman [?] her child and have no mercy on the one she bore from her womb? Even if this woman forgets, I will not forget you.
Look, I have drawn your walls on my hands, and you are always before me.
You will quickly be rebuilt after they tore you down, and those who devastated you will leave you.
Lift up your eyes and look around you! Look, they have gathered and come to you.
For after your devastation, downfall, and ruin, you will now be too cramped for those who live within you, and those who ravaged you will be far away.
Your children whom you lost will say in your hearing, “The land is too cramped for us. Make room for us where we can live.”
You will say in your heart, “Who bore these children for me? Look, I was barren and widowed. Who brought these up? Look, I was all alone. Where did these come from?”
This is what the Lord says: “Look, I will lift my hands toward the nations and set up a signal among the islands. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.”
Kings will be your servants, and queens will be your nurses.
Can anyone seize a giant's possessions? Will someone who takes captives unjustly escape?
Thus says the Lord: If anyone takes [?] captive, he takes your spoil; whoever overpowers a strong man will be saved.

Those who torment you will eat their own flesh and drink their own blood like new wine, and they will become drunk. Everyone living will know that I am the Lord who saved you and took you in, the Mighty One of Jacob.

Thus says the Lord: Where is your mother's certificate of divorce with which I sent her away? To which of my creditors did I sell you? Was it not because of your sins that I sold you, and because of your transgressions that I sent your mother away?
Look, I came, and there was no one; I called, and no one answered me.
I will cover the sky with darkness and clothe it in sackcloth.
The Lord God has given me a wise tongue, so that I may understand the word I speak.
The Lord's instruction opens my ears, and I do not reject him or argue with him.
I gave my back to whipping and my cheeks to blows. I did not turn my face away from the shame of being spat upon.
The Lord God became my helper. Therefore I was not ashamed. I made my face like solid rock, and I knew that I would not be put to shame.
For the one who vindicates me is near.
Look, the Lord helps me. Who will bring a charge against me? Look, all of you will wear out like a garment and be eaten as by moths.
Who among you fears the Lord? Let him listen to the voice of his servant.

Look, all of you kindle a fire and make its flame grow. Walk, then, in the light of your fire and the flame you have kindled. Because of me you have received this: all of you will lie down in your suffering.
Listen to me, all of you who pursue righteousness and seek the Lord. Look at the solid rock you quarried and the deep pit you dug.
Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah, who suffered labor pains for you. For he was only one when I called him, blessed him, loved him, and made him numerous.

And now I have comforted you, Jerusalem, and I will comfort all your fields. I will make your wilderness like a garden, and its fields like the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness will be found in it, Amen and the sound of praise.
Listen to me, listen to me, my people, and listen to my instruction, kings. For a law will go out from me, and my judgment will be a light to the nations.
My righteousness will come quickly, and my salvation will arrive, and the nations will trust in my arm.
Lift up your eyes and look at the heavens and the earth beneath them.
Listen to me, you who know justice, my people who have my law in your hearts. Do not fear people's insults; do not be terrified of them or be overcome.
For they will quickly wear out like a garment that [?], and they will become like food for worms. But my righteousness will stand forever, and my salvation from generation to generation.
Arise, arise, Jerusalem, and clothe yourself with the strength of your arm. Arise as in the days of old, from the creation of the world.
Was it not you who dried up the sea and dried up the waters of the great deep, and made the depths of the sea a road and a passage for those who were saved?
They rejoiced; the Lord brought them back, and they entered Zion with joy and everlasting gladness.
I am the one who comforts you. Consider, then, whom you yourself have feared: a mortal man, a human being who withers like grass.
But you forgot the Lord who created you, who made the heavens and established the earth. All your days you feared the anger of the one who tormented you.
For now that you have been saved, he will no longer exist, nor [?].
For I am the Lord your God, who stirs up the sea and makes its waves roar; my name is the Lord of hosts.
I will put my word in your mouth and cover you under the shadow of my hand, with which I spread out the heavens and established the earth. I will say to Zion, ‘You are my people.’
Arise, arise, Jerusalem, and stand up, you who have drunk from the Lord's hand the cup of his wrath. For you have drunk the cup of wrath that makes you fall, and you have drained it.
You have no one to comfort you among all the children you bore, and no one to stretch out his hand to you among all the children you raised.
And now these two things have befallen you. Who will comfort you? Disgrace and destruction, famine and slaughter—who, then, will comfort you?
Your children have grown faint and lie scattered along all the streets like [?] greens, filled with the wrath of the Lord and weakened by the Lord God.
Therefore listen to this, you who are afflicted and drunk, but not with wine.
This is what the Lord God, who judges for his people, says: “Look, I have taken from your hand the cup of your downfall, the cup of my wrath, and you will not drink it again.

I will put it into the hands of those who oppressed and humiliated you, who said to you, ‘Bend down so that we may walk over you.’ They made you lie on the ground on your belly, and everyone passing along the road walked over you.”
Rise, rise, Zion! Put on your strength, Zion! And you, Jerusalem, the holy city, put on your splendid garments. The uncircumcised and the unclean will no longer pass through you.
Shake off your dust and rise. Jerusalem, sit down. Cast the chain from your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
For this is what the Lord says: “I sold you for nothing, and it is not with gold that I will redeem you.”
As the Lord said: “My people first went down to Egypt and lived there as foreigners. Afterward they took them to the land of Persia in servitude.”
“And now, what has kept you here?” This is what the Lord says: “For they took my people for nothing. You were astonished and cried out.”
Therefore my people will know my name on that day, because I am the one who spoke, and I am here.
How beautiful on the mountains are those who announce news of peace, who proclaim good news!
For the voices of your watchmen have risen, and together they rejoice aloud. They will see eye to eye when the Lord has mercy on Zion.
Let the deserted places of Jerusalem burst into rejoicing together, for the Lord has had mercy on her and has saved Jerusalem.
The Lord will uncover his holy arm before all the nations, and all the nations will see the salvation of the Lord.
Go far away! Leave that place, and do not touch anything unclean. Come out from her midst and separate yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the Lord.
For you will not go out in turmoil, and you will not depart in flight.
Look, my servant will act wisely. He will be exalted and honored, and he will rejoice greatly.
Just as many will be astonished at you, so his appearance is strange compared with other people, and your glory compared with the children of Eve.
Many nations will be astonished at him, and kings will not open their mouths. For those who have not been told about him will come to know him, and those who have not heard will understand.
Lord, who has believed the message we spoke? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
We described him as a child before him, and as a root in thirsty ground. He has no attractive appearance or splendor. We saw him, and he had no attractive appearance or beauty.
His appearance was despised and lowlier than that of anyone else.
But he carried our sickness and suffered for us, while we regarded him as sick and stricken with suffering.
He was wounded because of our sins and suffered because of our transgressions. The discipline that brought us peace was upon him, and through his wounds we were healed.
We were all scattered like sheep. Each person went his own way and strayed.
But he did not open his mouth in his suffering.
For they will take him away to be judged.
I will give the wicked in exchange for his burial, and the rich in exchange for his death, because he committed no sin and no falsehood was found in his mouth.
The Lord wishes to cleanse him of his affliction.

The Lord wishes to remove suffering from his soul, to show him light, and to set him apart through his wisdom. He will justify the righteous one who serves many well, and he will wipe away their sins.

Therefore he will inherit Israel and take the mighty as spoils, because his life was given over to death and he was counted among sinners. He will bear the sins of many, and he was handed over because of their sins.
Rejoice, barren woman who does not bear children! Cry out and shout, you who have not suffered labor pains! For the widow has more children than the woman who has a husband.
Widen the supports of your tent; set up your enclosure and do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your stakes.
Spread out still further to the left and to the right, for your descendants will inherit nations, and you will inhabit desolate cities.
Do not fear, for you have been put to shame, and do not be ashamed, for they have despised you. You will forget your shame forever, and you will not remember the disgrace of your widowhood.
For the Lord who made you—the Lord of hosts is his name—is the God of Israel who saved you, whose name is proclaimed throughout the earth.
“The Lord did not call you as an abandoned and fainthearted woman, nor as a woman hated from her youth,” says your God.
They abandoned you for a few days, but with great mercy I will have compassion on you.
In a little anger I turned my face away from you, but with everlasting mercy I will have compassion on you, says the Lord who saved you.
This is my testimony concerning the waters in the days of Noah: just as I previously swore to the earth that it would no longer suffer wrath.
And that he would not strike the mountains or remove them, and that your hills would not be shaken.
And you shall read about the woman who is suffering, humbled, and sorrowful.
Your battlements will be of rubies, your gates of beryl, and your clothing of precious jewels.
All your children will be taught by the Lord, and your children will enjoy great peace.
And look, you will be built up in righteousness.
Look, foreigners will come from me and take refuge in you.
Look, I will create you—not like a smith who blows on the coals and brings forth a tool for his work. I created you for good, not for destruction.
Every word will rise up and accuse you, but you will overcome them all, and your people will inherit them.
Let those who are thirsty go to the water, and let those who have no gold go and buy. Let them drink wine and milk without gold.
Why do you buy with gold? Will your labor not bring you satisfaction? Listen to me, and you will eat blessings, and your souls will rejoice in blessing.
Follow my path and listen to me, and your souls will live in blessing. I will establish for David an everlasting ordinance of righteousness.
For look, I have made him trustworthy, a witness to the nations, a ruler and governor of the nations.
People who do not know you will call you, and people who do not recognize you will take refuge with you because of the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
Seek the Lord, and when you have found him, call upon him.
Let the sinner abandon his way and the unjust man his plans. Let him return to the Lord, and then he will have mercy on him, for he will abundantly forgive you your sins.
For my counsel is not like your counsel, and my path is not like your path, says the Lord.
As heaven is far from the earth, so my path is far from your paths, and my thoughts from your thoughts.
Just as rain and snow descend from heaven and do not cease until they have watered the earth, made it sprout and bear fruit, and given seed to the sower and grain for food.
So is my word that comes out of my mouth: it will not return until it has done everything I desired, and I will establish my way and my command.
For you will go out with joy and be taught with gladness.
Instead of thorns, a fir tree will grow, and instead of weeds, a myrtle tree.
This is what the Lord says: Preserve righteousness and justice, for my salvation has drawn near and arrived, and my mercy has been revealed.
Blessed is the person who does this and perseveres in it, who observes the Sabbaths without defiling them and does no injustice.
Let no foreigner who has come to the Lord say, “Will the Lord then separate me from his people?” And let no eunuch say, “I am like a dry tree.”
This is what the Lord said to the eunuchs: “If they observe my Sabbaths, choose what I desire, and persevere in my ordinances.”
I will give them, in my house and in my resting place, a place that brings them renown, better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not perish.

And to those from another people who have come to the Lord, subjected themselves to him, and loved the Lord’s name; to those who have become his male and female servants; and to all who keep my Sabbaths without profaning them and hold firmly to my ordinance.
I will bring them to my holy mountain and make them rejoice in my house of prayer.
And he is the one who gathers those of Israel who have been scattered.
Come, all you wild animals of the wilderness! Eat, all you wild animals of the wilderness!
Come and see how they have all become blind and have not thought about what counsel to give. They are mute dogs that cannot bark, dreaming on their beds and loving sleep.
They are all unclean dogs that are never satisfied.

You too saw how righteousness perished, but you did not consider it in your hearts. Righteous men have been taken away, and no one understood, for the righteous person was taken away from the presence of injustice.
His burial will be in peace, for they will take him away from their midst.
But you, come here, children of sinners, offspring of adulterers and adulteresses!
Whom have you mocked? Against whom have you opened your mouths, and against whom have you stretched out your tongues? Are you not children of sorcerers and offspring of evildoers?
You who delight in idols and offer sacrifices beneath leafy trees, and slaughter your children in the valleys among the clefts of the rocks.
This is your portion, and this is your inheritance: those to whom you poured out your drink offerings and to whom you offered your sacrifice.
On a great, high mountain you spread your bed; bring up your sacrifice there.
And you placed your [?] behind the door.
You multiplied your prostitution with them and befriended many who were far from you. You sent messengers and practiced deceit with them, and you were brought low as far as Sheol.
You labored in your travels, yet you did not say, “I will stop now, while I still have strength.” For you did this and were not ashamed before me.
Whom did you regard and fear, that you lied to me and did not remember me or consider me in your heart? I too ignored you, because you did not fear me.
Now I will expose my righteousness and your errors, which will not benefit you.
Let them save you when you cry out in your distress! Look, a storm will carry them all away, and the wind will sweep them away.
And he will say, “Clear a path before him, and remove the stones from the path of my people.”

This is what the Most High says, who dwells in the heights forever, whose name is Holy of Holies: the Lord who rests among the holy ones, gives endurance to the despised, and brings joy to the brokenhearted.
I will not punish you forever, nor will I always be angry with you, for the spirit comes from me, and I created every spirit.
Because of a small sin, I caused him pain and struck him. I turned my face away from him, and he became sorrowful and went away grieving.
Then I saw his ways, healed him, made him rejoice, and gave him righteous joy.
“Peace upon peace to those far away and those nearby,” says the Lord. “I will have mercy on them.”
But sinners will be tossed about like this and will find no rest.
“There is no joy for sinners,” says the Lord.
Cry out with all your strength and do not hold back. Raise your voice like a horn, and tell my people their sins and the house of Jacob their transgressions.
They seek me day after day and delight in knowing my ways, like a people who practice righteousness and do not abandon the judgment of their God.
They say, “Why have we fasted, but you have not seen us? Why have we afflicted ourselves, but you have not acknowledged us?” Because when you fast, you do as you please and collect your debts.
You make accusations, quarrel, exchange blows, and fight. You fast, yet you strike and oppress the poor. Why, then, do you fast for me as you do today, while you make the poor cry out and wail?

This is not the fast I have chosen, nor is it a day like this, when a person afflicts himself. Even if he bends his neck like a ring and lies down in sackcloth and dust, this is not a fast acceptable to the Lord.

“This is not the fast I have chosen,” says the Lord. “Rather, undo every bond of injustice, make peace, straighten everything crooked, set every distressed person free, and cancel every unjust document.”
Feed the hungry from your food until they are satisfied, and bring the poor person in and lodge him under the shelter of your house.
Then your light will break forth, and your garments will spring up quickly. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the Lord will cover you.
Then the Lord will hear you when you cry out. While you are still speaking, he will say to you, “Here I am,” once you have removed from yourself the bonds of injustice and grumbling.

If you do not strike others, but take some of the food you live on and feed the poor with it, and if you satisfy a hungry person, then your light will rise in the midst of darkness, and your darkness will become like daylight.
The Lord will be with you always. He will satisfy your heart’s desire and refresh your bones. You will be like a well-watered garden and like a pool whose water never dries up.
Your ancient ruins will be rebuilt, and your foundation will endure from generation to generation, forever and ever. You will be called a builder of [?] and a clearer of roads for habitation.

If you turn your foot back on the Sabbath so that you do not do as you please on the holy day, make the Sabbaths a delight, and consecrate them to the Lord, do not set your foot out to fulfill all your evil desires, and do not utter a harmful word from your mouth.
Trust in the Lord, and he will raise you up over the blessings of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
Is my hand unable to save? Does my ear not hear?
Do not your sins stand between you and the Lord? Because of your sins, I have turned my face away from you, so that he will not have mercy on you.
For your hands are full of blood, and your fingers of sin. With your lips you have spoken injustice, and your tongue has spoken sin.
There is no one who speaks righteousness or judges righteously.
They hatch serpents’ eggs and weave a spider’s thread. Whoever eats a serpent’s egg dies quickly, and if you break it open, a snake comes out.
A spider’s thread is of no use for clothing, and they cannot clothe themselves with their deeds, for their deeds are deeds of injustice.
Their feet run toward sin and hurry to shed blood, and they plot murder. Disgrace and destruction are in their paths.
They do not know the way of peace, and there is no righteousness in their paths. For the paths they walk are crooked, and they do not know peace.
Because of this, righteousness has drawn far away from them, and justice does not reach them. Their light has become darkness, and while they wait for light, they walk in darkness.
They grope along walls like a blind person who has no eyes. They fall in broad daylight as though it were midnight, and they groan like people who are dying.
They walk together like a dove and like a bear. We waited for judgment, but there is no one to save; he stands far away from us.
For our sins are many before you, and our transgressions stand against us.
We have sinned and lied to you, and we have stopped following our God. We have spoken injustice and denied you; we have conceived and planned sinful things in our hearts.
We have drawn away from righteousness and abandoned justice. Righteousness has disappeared from their paths, and they cannot walk in the open places.
They turned away from what is right and led their hearts astray so that they would not consider it.
He saw that there was no one, and he determined that there was no one to help him. He judged them with his arm and strengthened them by his mercy.
He put on righteousness like iron armor, placed a helmet of salvation on his head, and put on garments of vengeance.
He wrapped himself in a cloak of vengeance and retribution, with which he would put his enemies to shame.
Those in the west will fear the name of the Lord, and those where the sun rises will fear his glorious name.
A savior will come from Zion and remove sin from Jacob.

“This is their covenant from me,” says the Lord. “My Spirit is upon you, and I have put my word in your mouth. It will not depart from your mouth or from the mouth of your descendants,” says the Lord, “from now and forever.”
Shine, shine, Jerusalem! Your light has arrived, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
Look, darkness has covered the earth, and thick darkness is over the nations. But look, the Lord’s light and his glory have appeared over you.
Kings will walk by your light, and nations by your radiance.
Lift up your eyes, look around you, and see how your children have gathered. All your sons have come from far away, and your daughters are carried on shoulders.
Then you will see and be afraid, and your heart will tremble, because the wealth of the sea, that of the nations, and that in the streets will come to you.
They will bring herds of camels, and camels from Midian and Ephah will cover you.
The sheep of Kedar will gather, and they will bring rams from Nebaioth. They will offer choice sacrifices on my altar, and my house of prayer will be glorified.
Who are these who fly like a cloud and like a dove with her young?

The islands will put their hope in me, and the ships of Tarshish will come first and bring your children from a distant land, with their gold and silver, for the sake of the name of the Lord, the glorious Holy One of Israel.
The nations will build your walls, and their kings will stand before you. For in my anger I punished you, but in my mercy I brought you near.
Your gates will always be open; they will not be shut by day or by night. The wealth of the nations will enter you, and their kings will be brought in.
The kings who do not serve you will die, and the nations will be utterly destroyed.
The glory of Lebanon will come to you, with fir, pine, and cedar together, and the house of my sanctuary will be glorified.
They will come to you in fear, and the children of those who provoked you will bring gifts. You will be called Zion, the city of the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
For you were abandoned and hated, and you had no one to help you.
You will be nourished with the milk of the nations, and you will consume the wealth of nations and kings. You will know that I am the Lord who saved you and rescued you, the God of Israel.
Look, I will give you gold instead of bronze, silver instead of iron, bronze instead of wood, and iron instead of stone.
Violence will no longer be heard in your land, nor disgrace or destruction within your territory. Your walls will be called Salvation, and your gates will be engraved.
The sun will no longer give you light by day, nor will the moon shine for you by night. Instead, the Lord will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
Your sun will not set, and your moon will not disappear, because the Lord will be your light forever, and the days of your sorrow will pass away.
All your peoples will be righteous and will inherit the land forever. They will preserve the work of his hands for his glory.
Even those who are few will number ten thousand, and those who are small will become a strong nation. I, the Lord, will gather them at their appointed times.
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me. He has sent me to bring joy to the poor, to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom to captives, and to make the blind see.
And to proclaim the Lord’s year of favor and the day of judgment, to bring joy to those who mourn.

And to give those who mourn for Zion glory instead of dust, the perfume of joy to those who mourn, and a garment of glory instead of a downcast spirit. They will be called a generation of righteous people, a planting from the Lord for his glory.
They will rebuild the ancient ruins, raise up what was destroyed long ago, and restore cities that have lain ruined for generations.
Then other nations will come and tend your flocks, and foreigners will become farmers and vineyard keepers for them.
But you will be called priests of the Lord and servants of the Lord. You will consume the wealth of the nations and take pride in their riches.
They will inherit a double share of land, and everlasting joy will be upon their heads.
For I am the Lord, who loves justice and hates robbery and wrongdoing.
Their descendants will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples.
They will rejoice greatly in the Lord.
Like the produce of a flourishing field and like the seed of a garden, so the Lord will cause righteousness and joy to spring up before all the nations.
He will not remain silent for Zion’s sake, nor will he stop for Jerusalem’s sake, until my righteousness comes forth like light and my salvation shines like a lamp.
The nations will see your righteousness, and kings your glory. You will be called by a new name that the Lord has given you.
You will be a beautiful crown in the Lord’s hand and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.
You will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will no longer be called Desolate.
As a young man lives with a virgin, so your children will dwell. As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so the Lord will rejoice over you.
Jerusalem, I will station watchmen upon your walls, who will never be silent day or night as they remind the Lord.
Do not be silent before him until he establishes Jerusalem and makes her a joy upon the earth.

The Lord has sworn by his glory and by the power of his kingdom that he will no longer give your grain and your wheat to the enemy, and that enemies will never again drink the wine for which you have labored.
But whoever gathers it will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who gather it will drink it in my holy cities.
Go, enter through my gate! Clear a road for my people, remove the stones from the road, and raise a banner for the nations.
Look, the Lord is doing wonders to the ends of the earth.
You will be called a holy people whom the Lord has saved. And you will be called a holy city, one that is sought out and not abandoned.
Who is this who has arrived from Edom, with red garments from Bozrah—a proud man, mighty and fearsome in his clothing?
Why are your garments red, and why has your clothing come out of a winepress?
I have trodden the winepress alone, and no one from the nations was with me.
For their day of punishment has come upon them, and the day of redemption has arrived.
I saw that there was no one to help, and I knew that there was no one to offer support.
My scourge came upon them, and I poured out their blood on the ground.
I remembered the Lord's mercy in all his rewards.
And he said, “Are they not my people and my children? If they do not deny me, I will save them”
from all their distress.
But they rebelled against him and angered the Holy Spirit.
And he remembered the days of old.
Who led them by Moses' right hand and by his glorious arm; the water stood firm before him, and he made for himself an everlasting name.
He led them through the midst of the deep like a horse in the wilderness, and they did not grow weary.
And like livestock in a field.
Turn from heaven and look from your holy and glorious dwelling.
You are our Father. Abraham did not know us, and Israel did not acknowledge us. But you are our Father; save us. From ancient times your name has been upon us.
Why, Lord, have you led us astray from your way and hardened our hearts so that we do not fear you? Return for the sake of your servants and the people of your inheritance.
So that we may receive a small portion of your inheritance on your holy mountain.
For we have become as we were long ago, when you did not rule over us and when your name was not called over us.
If only you would open the heavens! The mountains would tremble before you and shake.
As wax melts before fire, so fire will consume your enemies, and your name will be made known among them.
And when you display your glory, the mountains tremble.
Since the creation of the world, we have neither seen nor heard of another God besides you. You show your mercy to those who hope for your grace.
Those who persevere in your righteousness and those who remember your ways will find you.
We have all become unclean, and all our righteousness is like a menstrual cloth. We have fallen like leaves because of our sins.
There is no one who calls on your name, and they do not remember you.
Even now, you are our Lord and our Father. We are clay, and you formed us; we are all the work of your hands.
Do not be exceedingly angry with us, and do not remember our sins against us. Now look upon us, for we are all your people.
For your sanctuary has been laid waste; Zion has become a ruin, and Jerusalem a curse.
Your holy house has been burned with fire, our glory, where our fathers offered blessing, and all our possessions have fallen.
And in all this you bore with us, Lord, and remained silent and greatly humbled us.
Those who did not seek me found me, and I revealed myself to those who did not ask for me.
All day long I stretch out my hands to a rebellious and faithless people, who did not walk in the way of righteousness but followed their sins.
This is the people who continually rebelled against me.
They sleep in the caves of dreamers, eat swine’s flesh, and defile the blood of their sacrifices and all their vessels.
They say, “Stay away from me and do not come near me, for I am pure.”
Look, it is written before me. It will not remain silent until I repay, take vengeance, and return their recompense into their laps.
Their sins and those of their fathers, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: Just as a grape is found in a cluster and people say, “Do not destroy it, for the Lord’s blessing is upon it,” so I will act for the sake of my servant; because of him I will not destroy.
I will bring forth descendants of Jacob and descendants of Judah, and they will inherit my holy mountain. My chosen ones and my servants will inherit it and live there.
They will dwell among trees and pasture enclosures, and in the valleys of Achor there will be cattle enclosures for my people who sought me.
But you who abandoned me and forgot my holy mountain set a table for demons and pour out drink for idols, filling their cups.

I will hand you over to war, and you will all die by slaughter. For I called you, and you did not answer me; I spoke to you, and you turned a deaf ear to me. You did evil before me, and you did not want me to save you.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Those who serve me will eat, but you will go hungry. Those who serve me will drink, but you will be thirsty. Those who serve me will rejoice, but you will be disgraced.
Those who serve me will rejoice with gladness, but you will cry out in the pain of your hearts and wail in the anguish of your souls.
For you have left your name and filled my chosen ones with it. But the Lord will destroy you, and he will give a new name to those who serve me.
They will be blessed upon the earth, for they will bless the God of righteousness; and those who swear upon the earth will swear by the God of righteousness.
For there will be a new heaven and a new earth. The former things will no longer be remembered or come into their minds.
Instead, they will find joy and gladness within her. I will make Jerusalem a joy, and bring gladness among my people.
I will be glad over Jerusalem and rejoice over my people. The sound of weeping and the sound of wailing will no longer be heard within her.
There will no longer be an infant who lives only a few days, or a wicked person who does not complete his allotted time.
They will build houses and live in them; they will plant vines and eat their fruit.

They will not build houses for others to live in, or plant for others to eat. The days of my people will be like the days of the tree of life, and my chosen ones will grow old amid the works of their hands.
They will no longer labor in vain or bear children for a curse, for they are descendants blessed by the Lord, and their children will be with them.
Before they call, I will give to them; while they are still speaking, I will say to them, “Here I am.”

At that time wolves and sheep will graze together, and the lion will eat grass like an ox. Dust will be the serpent’s food. There will be no one who harms and no one who destroys on my holy mountain, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
All this is the work of my hands, and all this belongs to me, says the Lord.

A sinner who sacrifices an ox to me is like someone who slaughters a dog for me. Someone who brings me fine flour is like someone who brings pig’s blood, and someone who offers incense in remembrance of me is like someone who blasphemes.
I too will choose to disgrace them and take vengeance on them for their sins.
Hear the word of the Lord, you who tremble at his word. Say to those who hate you, “Our brothers,” so that the Lord’s name may be glorified and he may reveal your joy; but they will be put to shame.
A sound of shouting from the city, a voice from the temple—the voice of the Lord, who takes vengeance on his enemies.
She gives birth without suffering labor pains, she who is in labor, and she bore a male child.
Who has heard anything like this, and who has seen anything like this? Has the earth given birth in a single hour? Are nations born all at once? For Zion has given birth to children.
“I gave you joy, but you did not remember me,” says the Lord.
Rejoice, Jerusalem, and be glad, all who love her! Rejoice with joy, all of you who mourned for her!
So that you may nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breasts, so that you may be held close and rejoice in her glory.
This is what the Lord says: “Look, I am bringing them peace like a river, and the glory of the nations like the waves of the sea.”
“As a mother comforts, so I will comfort you in Jerusalem.”
You will see, and your hearts will rejoice, and your bones will flourish like grass.
Look, the Lord is coming like fire, and his chariots like a whirlwind, to take vengeance on them in his anger, and to rebuke them with blazing fire.
For all the earth will be judged by the Lord’s fire, and every living being by his spear; for many will be slain by the Lord.
“Those who purify and cleanse themselves in the gardens and in the porticoes, while eating pork, unclean things, and mice, will perish together,” says the Lord.
“I know their deeds and their thoughts. Look, I am coming to gather all the nations, and they will come and see my glory.”

“I will give them a sign, and I will send those among them who escaped death to the nations—to Tarshish, Put, Lud, Meshech, Tubal, and Greece, and to distant islands that have not heard of my deeds or seen my glory.”

“They will bring their brothers from every region as an offering to the Lord, on horses, in chariots and litters, and on camels and mules, into the holy city,” says the Lord, “just as the children of Israel brought their sacrifices to me with song into the house of the Lord.”
“I will also take some of them as priests and Levites,” says the Lord.
“Just as the new heaven and the new earth that I make will remain before me,” says the Lord, “so your descendants and your name will endure.”
“Month after month and Sabbath after Sabbath, every living being will come before me and worship me in Jerusalem,” says the Lord.
“They will go out and see the corpses of those who rebelled against me. Their worm does not sleep, and their fire is not extinguished; and they will be a spectacle to all flesh.”
